summary: Checkpoints 1–5 (Claude Code cc-39fac3), under RS-08. R21.2 is source_decomposed; R21.1, R21.3, R21.4 and R21.5 are partial; R21.6 is not read. The source is Skinner–Wiles, Residually reducible representations and modular forms (Publ. IHÉS 89, 1999), §§3.1–3.5. R21.1 (8 nodes) applies PadicFamilies L0a's ordinary projector to the definite quaternionic forms of HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.3: Skinner–Wiles' exponent p^n(p^m − 1) gives L0a's projector; it kills norm-factoring forms; the nearly ordinary Hecke algebra T_∞(U, 𝒪) over Λ′_𝒪; the stabiliser-weighted pairing with Hecke adjoints, traces between levels, the Γ₀(p^a) level drop, and the Pontryagin duality M_∞ ≅ H_∞^∨. R21.2 (7 nodes) keeps the nearly ordinary and Eisenstein statements: v-good lines and nearly ordinary representations, the two definitions of the Hecke algebra, permissible (Eisenstein) maximal ideals, their existence from the Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-function (Proposition 3.18), the weight algebra Λ_𝒪 at m, finiteness and freeness at m (Lemma 3.10), and freeness over an auxiliary Δ_w-group (Lemma 3.19). Hida's control over Λ′_𝒪 is requested from PadicFamilies L5. Two misprints are recorded (E1: the rank of Λ_𝒪 over Λ′_𝒪 is p^{Σ r_j}, not Σ r_j). Checkpoint 2 plans R21.3 (19 nodes) from Skinner–Wiles §§2 and 3.3: deformation data, the nearly ordinary deformation rings R_𝒟 with their presentation and dimension bound, Wiles pseudo-representations and pseudo-deformation rings with the lifting Proposition 2.15, the Λ_𝒪-structures, Hida's family representation ρ_Q, the pseudo-representation into T_m with R_{𝒟^ps} ↠ T_m, and the level, type and twisting statements. Two more misprints: E3 (Lemma 3.11 omits (β_i − α_i)^{−1}) and E4 ((3.7) inverts Ψ_P at T_0(𝔭_i)). Checkpoint 3 completes R21.2 (Proposition 3.20, Lemma 3.21, the rings T_𝒟 and T^min with Proposition 3.23, the §3.7 duality, the quaternionic Ihara lemma and Lemmas 3.27–3.29), adds §2.2's reducible locus to R21.3, and starts R21.4 with pro-modular primes, good pairs, nice primes, (P1)/(P2), Corollary A.2 (Raynaud's connectedness theorem is a gap) and the key Proposition 4.1. E5 and E6 are cross-reference misprints. Checkpoint 4 adds Proposition 4.2, the reduction of (P1) to Proposition 8.1 (Skinner–Wiles §§5–8, a temporary gap until the next checkpoint) and the Main Theorem to R21.4, and Theorems A and B with Hypothesis H to R21.5 (Washington's and Waldschmidt's theorems are gaps). E7: a label misprint. Checkpoint 5 plans Skinner–Wiles §§5–8 (formal patching, characteristic-p Selmer estimates and auxiliary primes, R = T at nice primes of minimal level and in general), closing the temporary gap; E8: 'Proposition 7.2' for 7.3.

nodes.title: Skinner–Wiles' exponent gives the factorial projector
nodes.statement: Let A be an 𝒪-algebra that is a finite 𝒪-module and t ∈ A. Let m be divisible by [k_i : F_p] for every residue field k_i of the commutative finite 𝒪-algebra 𝒪[t]. Then lim_{n→∞} t^{p^n(p^m − 1)} exists in A and equals the ordinary idempotent e_t = lim_n t^{n!} of PadicFamilies L0a. In particular Skinner–Wiles' operator e = lim_n T₀(p)^{p^n(p^m−1)} is L0a's ordinary projector of T₀(p).
hypotheses: 𝒪 complete with finite residue field; A finite over 𝒪 (so 𝒪[t] is a finite product of complete local rings).
proofSteps: 𝒪[t] = ∏_i 𝒪[t]_{m_i}, each factor complete local with residue field k_i ⊆ F_{p^m}.
If t is a unit in the i-th factor, t^{p^m−1} ∈ 1 + m_i, and (1 + x)^{p^n} ∈ 1 + m_i^{n+1} for x ∈ m_i since p ∈ m_i; so t^{p^n(p^m−1)} → 1 there. If t ∈ m_i, t^N → 0.
The limit is therefore the idempotent of the factors where t is a unit, which is e_t by L0a's characterisation (t invertible on e_tA, topologically nilpotent on (1 − e_t)A).
acceptance: No second projector API is built: SW's exponent is compared with L0a's n!.

nodes.title: Hida's ordinary projector on definite quaternionic forms
nodes.statement: F is a totally real field of even degree d, p an odd prime, D/F the quaternion algebra ramified exactly at the infinite places, X(U) = D^×\G^D(A_f)/U and H⁰(X(U), R) the R-valued functions on it (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.3), for open compact U ⊆ GL₂(𝒪_F ⊗ Ẑ) with U_v = GL₂(𝒪_{F,v}) for v | p; U_a = U ∩ U(p^a), U⁰_a = U ∩ U₀(p^a). 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite extension K of ℚ_p with uniformiser π and residue field k. Let T₀(p) = [U_a (1 0; 0 ϖ_p) U_a] on H⁰(X(U_a), R), ϖ_p the finite idele with a uniformiser at each v | p and 1 elsewhere. For every 𝒪-module R that is finite as a set, e := lim_n T₀(p)^{p^n(p^m−1)} (m sufficiently divisible) is L0a's ordinary projector of T₀(p); for R = 𝒪 it is L0a's adic projector on the finite free module H⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪), and for R = K/𝒪 = colim 𝒪/πⁿ it is the colimit of the finite projectors. e is an idempotent in End_𝒪(H⁰(X(U_a), R)) commuting with the Hecke algebra T(U_a, 𝒪) generated by T₀(p), T₀(p_i) (i = 1, …, t), G(U_a) and T(ℓ), S(ℓ) for ℓ ∤ p with U_ℓ = GL₂(𝒪_{F,ℓ}); it commutes with change of coefficients R → R′ and with the level-change maps (pullback and trace) between U_b and U_a, b ≥ a.
hypotheses: [F : ℚ] even, so that D exists (a quaternion algebra is ramified at an even number of places).
U_v = GL₂(𝒪_{F,v}) for v | p; the Hecke operators are those of R18.3.
proofSteps: For R finite apply L0a/finite-ordinary-projector to T₀(p); by projector-exponent-comparison SW's exponent gives the same idempotent.
For R = 𝒪, H⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪) is finite free (R18.3); apply L0a/adic-instance. For R = K/𝒪 take the colimit over 𝒪/πⁿ, using naturality for the inclusions.
Commutation with Hecke operators, coefficient change, pullback and trace: these maps commute with T₀(p) (R18.3 and ordinary-trace-compatibility), so L0a/ordinary-projector-natural applies.
acceptance: The projector is defined on integral or torsion coefficients and extended K-linearly, never by a limit in End_K.
Level change is compatible with e in both directions (pullback and trace).

nodes.title: The ordinary projector kills norm-factoring forms
nodes.statement: Let I^D(U_a, ℤ) ⊆ H⁰(X(U_a), ℤ) be the functions factoring through the reduced norm ν_D : G^D(A_f)/U_a → A_f^×/ν_D(U_a), for a ≥ 1. Then e annihilates I^D(U_a, ℤ) ⊗ R for every 𝒪-module R.
hypotheses: a ≥ 1, so that U_{a,v} is pro-p at each v | p.
proofSteps: For f = h ∘ ν_D and g = (1 0; 0 ϖ_p), T₀(p)f(x) = Σ_i f(x g_i) over U_a g U_a = ⊔ g_i U_a, and ν_D(x g_i) ≡ ν_D(x)ν_D(ϖ_p) mod ν_D(U_a) for all i.
So T₀(p)f = N·(f translated by ν_D(ϖ_p)) with N = [U_a : U_a ∩ gU_ag^{−1}], a positive power of p.
Hence T₀(p) is topologically nilpotent on I^D(U_a, ℤ) ⊗ R and e = lim T₀(p)^{p^n(p^m−1)} is 0 there.
acceptance: Only the cuspidal quotient S^D(U_a) = H⁰/I^D survives the projector; the Jacquet–Langlands comparison is on S^D.

nodes.title: The nearly ordinary Hecke algebra T_∞(U, 𝒪)
nodes.statement: F is a totally real field of even degree d, p an odd prime, D/F the quaternion algebra ramified exactly at the infinite places, X(U) = D^×\G^D(A_f)/U and H⁰(X(U), R) the R-valued functions on it (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.3), for open compact U ⊆ GL₂(𝒪_F ⊗ Ẑ) with U_v = GL₂(𝒪_{F,v}) for v | p; U_a = U ∩ U(p^a), U⁰_a = U ∩ U₀(p^a). 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite extension K of ℚ_p with uniformiser π and residue field k. T(U_a, 𝒪) ⊆ End_𝒪(H⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪)) is generated over 𝒪 by T₀(p), T₀(p_i), G(U_a), T(ℓ) and S(ℓ) (ℓ ∤ p, U_ℓ maximal), and T₂(U_a, 𝒪) := eT(U_a, 𝒪), the image of T(U_a, 𝒪) in End_𝒪(eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪)). By the Jacquet–Langlands–Shimizu isomorphism S^D(U) ≅ S₂(U) this is Skinner–Wiles' eT*₂(U_a, 𝒪). The maps T₂(U_b, 𝒪) → T₂(U_a, 𝒪) (b ≥ a) are surjective, and T_∞(U, 𝒪) := lim_a T₂(U_a, 𝒪). With G(U) = lim_a G(U_a) ≅ (𝒪_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× × Z(U) there is a continuous 𝒪[[G(U)]] → T_∞(U, 𝒪), and T_∞(U, 𝒪) is an algebra over Λ′_𝒪 = 𝒪[[X_1, …, X_{δ_F}, Y^{(1)}_1, …, Y^{(t)}_{d_t}]] via X_i ↦ S_{x_i} − 1 and Y^{(i)}_j ↦ T_{y^{(i)}_j} − 1, where the x_i generate a maximal ℤ_p-free summand of Z(U) and the y^{(i)}_j a free summand of rank d_i of 𝒰_{v_i}.
hypotheses: [F : ℚ] even; G(U_a) ≅ (𝒪_F/p^a)^× × Z(U_a) via (a b; c d) ↦ (∏_{v|p}(a^{−1}d)_v, a).
proofSteps: The generators commute (R18.3), so T(U_a, 𝒪) is a commutative finite 𝒪-algebra; e ∈ T(U_a, 𝒪) by projector-exponent-comparison, and eT(U_a, 𝒪) acts faithfully on eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪).
The comparison with forms on GL₂ is R17.3 on S^D = H⁰/I^D, which e sees entirely (ordinary-part-kills-norm-forms).
Pullback H⁰(X(U_a)) → H⁰(X(U_b)) is Hecke-equivariant (G(U_b) → G(U_a)), so restriction of operators gives T₂(U_b, 𝒪) → T₂(U_a, 𝒪), surjective because generators map to generators.
The group elements give compatible maps 𝒪[G(U_a)] → T₂(U_a, 𝒪), hence 𝒪[[G(U)]] → T_∞(U, 𝒪) (the completed group ring of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1).
acceptance: Λ′_𝒪 has δ_F variables X_i for the ℤ_p-free part of Z(U) and d = Σ d_i variables Y for the torus at p, after the choices of x_i and y^{(i)}_j; no variable is attached to the class group.

nodes.title: The stabiliser-weighted pairing and Hecke adjoints
nodes.statement: For open compact U put Ū = U/(U ∩ F^×) and, for x ∈ G^D(A_f), c_U(x) = #{u ∈ Ū : xu = x} in D^×\G^D(A_f). For an 𝒪-algebra R in which every c_U(x) is invertible, ⟨f, g⟩_U = Σ_{x ∈ X(U)} c_U(x)^{−1} f(x)g(x) is a perfect R-bilinear pairing on H⁰(X(U), R), and f ↦ ⟨f, ·⟩_U is an isomorphism H⁰(X(U), R) ≅ Hom_R(H⁰(X(U), R), R) functorial in R. It satisfies ⟨[UgU]f, h⟩_U = ⟨f, [Ug^{−1}U]h⟩_U for g ∈ G^D(A_f), so every t ∈ T(U_a, 𝒪) has an adjoint t⁺, and t ↦ t⁺ is an 𝒪-algebra isomorphism T(U_a, 𝒪) ≅ T⁺(U_a, 𝒪). Writing H⁰(X(U_a), R)⁺ for H⁰ with t acting by t⁺, the pairing induces a perfect pairing of T₂(U_a, 𝒪)-modules eH⁰(X(U_a), R) × eH⁰(X(U_a), R)⁺ → R.
hypotheses: Every c_U(x) invertible in R (automatic for R an 𝒪-algebra once a is large, R18.3).
proofSteps: c_U(x) is the order of the finite stabiliser of x (D^× discrete, Ū compact modulo the centre).
Adjointness: expand both sides over the single cosets of UgU and Ug^{−1}U and change variables; the weights c_U account for the non-free points.
e⁺ is the adjoint idempotent; eH⁰ and (1 − e⁺)H⁰ are orthogonal, so the pairing restricts to a perfect pairing between eH⁰ and e⁺H⁰ = eH⁰(X(U_a), R)⁺.
acceptance: The pairing is not Hecke-equivariant; only the twisted module H⁰(·)⁺ is paired.

nodes.title: Trace maps between levels
nodes.statement: For V ⊆ U open compact and Ū = ⊔_i V̄x_i, tr(V, U) : H⁰(X(V), R) → H⁰(X(U), R), tr(V, U)f(x) = Σ_i f(x x_i^{−1}). For V = U_b, U = U_a (b ≥ a) it is independent of the coset representatives and commutes with t and t⁺ for t ∈ T₂(U_b, 𝒪) (acting on level U_a through the transition map), hence with e; and whenever both pairings are defined, ⟨f, tr(V, U)h⟩_U = ⟨f|_V, h⟩_V for f ∈ H⁰(X(U), R) and h ∈ H⁰(X(V), R): restriction and trace are adjoint.
hypotheses: b ≥ a (U_b is normal in U_a, so the representatives can be chosen in U_a and the sum is well defined).
proofSteps: Independence: U_b is normal in U_a and f is right U_b-invariant.
Hecke compatibility: T₀(p), T₀(p_i), T(ℓ), S(ℓ) and G(U_b) commute with right translation by U_a/U_b.
Adjunction: split the sum over X(V) along the fibres of X(V) → X(U); the stabiliser weights match (c_V(y) sums to c_U(x)·#fibre).
acceptance: The traces are the transition maps of M_∞; the pullbacks are those of H_∞.

nodes.statement: For a ≥ 2, U⁰_a (1 0; 0 ϖ_p) U⁰_a = U⁰_a (1 0; 0 ϖ_p) U⁰_{a−1}; hence T₀(p) maps H⁰(X(U⁰_a), K/𝒪) into H⁰(X(U⁰_{a−1}), K/𝒪) and eH⁰(X(U⁰_a), K/𝒪) = eH⁰(X(U⁰_1), K/𝒪). Moreover H⁰(X(U⁰_a), K/𝒪) = H⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪)^{G(U_a)}.
hypotheses: a ≥ 2; U⁰_a = U ∩ U₀(p^a).
proofSteps: So gU⁰_{a−1} = N⁻(p^a)gU⁰_a ⊆ U⁰_a g U⁰_a, giving the double-coset identity and the level drop of T₀(p).
e is a limit of powers of T₀(p), so its image lies in level U⁰_{a−1}, and by induction in level U⁰_1.
acceptance: The identity fails for a = 1 (U⁰_0 = U is not N⁻·U⁰_1).

nodes.title: Pontryagin duality for the ordinary quaternionic towers
nodes.statement: Put H_∞(U) = lim→_a eH⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪) and H⁺_∞(U) = lim→_a eH⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪)⁺ along pullbacks, and M_∞(U) = lim←_a eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪)⁺, M⁺_∞(U) = lim←_a eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪) along the traces tr(U_b, U_a). These are T_∞(U, 𝒪)-modules, and since c_{U_a}(x) = 1 for all x once a is large, the pairings give T_∞(U, 𝒪)-isomorphisms M_∞(U) ≅ Hom_𝒪(H_∞(U), K/𝒪) and M⁺_∞(U) ≅ Hom_𝒪(H⁺_∞(U), K/𝒪).
hypotheses: c_{U_a}(x) = 1 for all x ∈ X(U_a) for a large (R18.3 stabilisers).
proofSteps: For large a the ordinary pairing identifies eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪)⁺ with Hom_𝒪(eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪), 𝒪), compatibly with trace and restriction (ordinary-trace-compatibility).
For L finite free, Hom_𝒪(L, 𝒪) ≅ Hom_𝒪(L ⊗ K/𝒪, K/𝒪), and eH⁰(X(U_a), K/𝒪) = eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪) ⊗ K/𝒪.
Hom_𝒪(−, K/𝒪) turns the colimit H_∞ into the limit, giving M_∞(U) ≅ Hom_𝒪(H_∞(U), K/𝒪); likewise for ⁺.
acceptance: The duality is between M_∞ (twisted action) and H_∞ (untwisted); do not drop the ⁺.
Skinner–Wiles write H⁺_∞(U_a) for the limit H⁺_∞(U) (E2).

nodes.title: Nearly ordinary automorphic representations
nodes.statement: Let k = Σ_τ k_ττ with every k_τ ≥ 2, π ∈ Π_k(U_a) a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(A_F) of weight k with V_π^{U_a} ≠ 0, and v | p with prime p_v. A line in V_{π,v}^{U_{a,v}} on which T₀(p_v) acts through an element of F̄ that is a unit in the ring of integers of Q̄_p is unique if it exists; it is called v-good. A v-good line exists iff π_v is a principal series π(η_v|·|_v^{−1/2}, ξ_v|·|_v^{−1/2}) or a special representation π(ξ_v|·|_v^{−1/2}, ξ_v|·|_v^{1/2}) with λ_v^{−v}ξ_v(λ_v^{−1}) a p-adic unit (λ_v the uniformiser used in T₀(p_v)). π is nearly ordinary if a v-good line exists for every v | p, and ordinary if moreover ξ_v is unramified for every v | p; a newform is (nearly) ordinary if its automorphic representation is. Π^{n.o.}_k(U_a) ⊆ Π_k(U_a) is the set of nearly ordinary π (Skinner–Wiles write Π^ord_k(U_a)).
hypotheses: F totally real of any degree (the definition does not need the quaternion algebra); v = (v_τ) with m + 2v ∈ ℤt, m = k − 2t, as in Skinner–Wiles §3.1.
proofSteps: Uniqueness and the criterion are Hida's classification of unit U_p-eigenlines ([H3, Corollary 2.2]) on the local newform theory of R16.6.
acceptance: Keep 'nearly ordinary' (ξ_v arbitrary) and 'ordinary' (ξ_v unramified) apart: twisting by a character ramified at v | p preserves the first but not the second.

nodes.title: The two definitions of the nearly ordinary Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: For parallel k and U_v = GL₂(𝒪_{F,v}) (v | p): let S*_k(U_a) be spanned by vectors w(π) = ⊗_v w(π, v) with w(π, v) spanning the v-good line, π ∈ Π^{n.o.}_k(U_a), and T_k(U_a) ⊆ End(S*_k(U_a)) the ℤ_p-algebra generated by the Hecke operators. Then T_k(U_a) is finite, flat, commutative and reduced, T_k(U_a) ↪ ∏_{π ∈ Π^{n.o.}_k(U_a)} Q̄_p, and T_k(U_a) ⊗ 𝒪 = eT*_k(U_a, 𝒪), since eV_π^{U_a} = 0 for π ∉ Π^{n.o.}_k(U_a) and eV_π^{U_a} = {⊗x_v : x_v spans a v-good line for every v | p} otherwise. For k = 2 this is T₂(U_a, 𝒪) of R21.1, and 𝒪-algebra maps λ : T_∞(U, 𝒪) → Q̄_p whose restrictions to Z(U) and to (𝒪_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× have finite order factor through some T₂(U_a, 𝒪) and correspond to π ∈ ⋃_a Π^{n.o.}_2(U_a) with an eigenvector in the v-good lines.
hypotheses: Parallel weight for the comparison with e; general weights through Hida's control (Skinner–Wiles Proposition 3.7, requested from PadicFamilies L5).
proofSteps: e acts on V_π^{U_a} = ⊗_v V_{π,v}^{U_{a,v}} factor by factor at v | p; on each factor it is the projector onto the unit-eigenvalue line of T₀(p_v), which is the v-good line or 0.
Reducedness and the injection come from the semisimplicity of the Hecke action on S*_k with one-dimensional eigenspaces w(π).
A weight-two λ with finite-order restrictions factors through a finite level by the definition of T_∞ and corresponds to the unique π whose v-good vector has those eigenvalues.
acceptance: The comparison is between the same classical newform on GL₂ and on D (through R21.1's Jacquet–Langlands step); the Galois family is compared in R21.3.

nodes.title: Permissible (Eisenstein) maximal ideals
nodes.statement: Let k be a finite field of characteristic p and χ : Gal(F̄/F) → k^× a character with χ|_{D_{v_i}} ≠ 1 for every v_i | p and χ(c_j) = −1 for every complex conjugation c_j; let 𝒪 have residue field k, χ̃ the Teichmüller lift and ω the Teichmüller character. A maximal ideal m of T_∞(U, 𝒪) is permissible if (3.9): m ∩ 𝒪[[G(U)]] is the maximal ideal of the character G(U) → Z(U) --χω^{−1}--> k; m contains T₀(p_i) − 1 for i = 1, …, t; and m contains T(ℓ) − 1 − χ̃(Frob_ℓ) for every ℓ ∤ p with U_ℓ = GL₂(𝒪_{F,ℓ}). The same conditions define permissible maximal ideals of T₂(U_a, 𝒪), and each determines one of T_∞(U, 𝒪).
hypotheses: p odd; F of even degree (T_∞ is built from D); χ totally odd and p-distinguished (χ|_{D_v} ≠ 1 at every v | p).
proofSteps: Skinner–Wiles' first definition replaces the third condition by ρ̄_m ≅ χ ⊕ 1 for the residual pseudo-representation; the two agree by Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt once R21.3 supplies ρ̄_m (p > 2).
acceptance: Uniqueness of a permissible ideal and the value of S(ℓ) mod m use det ρ̄_m = χ; they are proved in R21.3/permissible-residual-comparison, not from (3.9) alone.

nodes.title: Existence of permissible maximal ideals
nodes.statement: Let n be the prime-to-p part of the conductor of χω^{−1}; for ℓ | n let ℓ^{r(ℓ)} ∥ n and Δ_ℓ be the Sylow p-subgroup of (𝒪_F/ℓ^{r(ℓ)})^×. Let U^χ = ∏_ℓ U^χ_ℓ with U^χ_ℓ = {(a b; c d) ∈ GL₂(𝒪_{F,ℓ}) : c ∈ ℓ^{r(ℓ)}, a mod ℓ^{r(ℓ)} ∈ Δ_ℓ} for ℓ | n and GL₂(𝒪_{F,ℓ}) otherwise, and let L_p(F, s, χω) be the Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-function. If ord_π(L_p(F, −1, χω)) > 0, then some T₂(U^χ_a, 𝒪), and hence T_∞(U^χ, 𝒪), has a permissible maximal ideal.
hypotheses: F of even degree; χ totally odd and p-distinguished, as in permissible-maximal-ideal.
proofSteps: Put ψ = χω^{−1}. The Eisenstein series E_n(φ₁, φ₂) ∈ M_n(pn, ψ) with Dirichlet series L(F, s, φ₁)L(F, s − n + 1, φ₂) span a complement of S_n(n, ψ), and a_i(E_n(1, ψ), 0) = 2^{−d}L(F, 1 − n, ψ)Nm(t_i)^{n/2} (3.10) (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3).

With f = ord_p(ε(γ) − 1), choose n = 2 + p^f(p − 1)m so large that Chai's form g ∈ M_n(np, ψ) ∩ M_n(np, 𝒪) with a_i(g, 0) = 2^{−d}Nm(t_i)^{n/2} (3.11) exists; the p-adic L-function gives ord_π(L(F, 1 − n, ψ)) > 0, so E₀ = E_n(1, ψ) is integral and f₀ = L(F, 1 − n, ψ)g − E₀ has all constant terms 0.

E₁ = eE₀ is the eigenform with Dirichlet series ζ_F(s)L^{(p)}(s − n + 1, ψ); for its idempotent ε₀, the Eisenstein part of ε₀f₀ is a combination of E_n(λ, λ^{−1}ψ) with zero constant terms, hence 0 (Wiles [W3, Prop. 1.6]).
So F₁ = ε₀ef₀ is a cusp form with F₁ ≡ E₁ ≢ 0 mod π, giving an ordinary newform f₁ congruent to E₁ at the Dirichlet coefficients.

Wiles' Λ-adic forms ([W2, Theorem 1.4.1], PadicFamilies L5) give a weight-two p-stabilised newform f₂ ∈ S₂(np^a, ψ) with the same congruence; it spans v-good lines (nearly-ordinary-hecke-algebra-comparison), and its maximal ideal satisfies (3.9).
Local–global compatibility at ℓ | n ([W2, Theorem 2.1.3] or (3.3); AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.4) puts π_{f₂} in Π^{n.o.}_2(U^χ_a).
acceptance: The hypothesis is on the p-adic L-value at s = −1; the congruence is built in weight n ≡ 2 mod (p − 1)p^f and moved to weight 2 by Hida theory, not by a weight-two construction.
The maximal ideal lives at level U^χ (Γ₀-type at n with Δ-reduced diagonal), not at U₁(n).

nodes.title: The weight algebra at a permissible maximal ideal
nodes.statement: Let m be a permissible maximal ideal of T_∞(U, 𝒪) and γ_1, …, γ_{δ_F} ∈ Gal(F̄/F), r_1, …, r_{δ_F} as in Skinner–Wiles §2.5 (the γ_j generate a free summand G₀ of Gal(L₀/F) and the γ_j^{p^{r_j}} generate I₀, with images x_j ∈ Z(U)). Let D : Gal(F̄/F) → T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m^× be the continuous character given by the central action composed with reciprocity, times ε; so D(Frob_ℓ) = S(ℓ)Nm(ℓ) for ℓ ∤ np and D(x) = S_xε(x) on Z(U) (Skinner–Wiles' det ρ^mod_m). Then T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m is an algebra over Λ_𝒪 = 𝒪[[T_1, …, T_{δ_F}, Y^{(i)}_j]] via 1 + Y^{(i)}_j ↦ T_{y^{(i)}_j} and 1 + T_j ↦ D(γ_j), and the map Λ′_𝒪 → Λ_𝒪, 1 + X_j ↦ (1 + T_j)^{p^{r_j}}ε(γ_j^{−p^{r_j}}), Y ↦ Y, is compatible with the Λ′_𝒪-structure of R21.1 and makes Λ_𝒪 a free Λ′_𝒪-module of rank p^{Σ_j r_j}.
hypotheses: m permissible; the choices of γ_j, r_j and y^{(i)}_j of Skinner–Wiles §2.5.
proofSteps: The centre A_f^× acts on H⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪) through the finite group A_f^×/F^×(U_a ∩ A_f^×); with class field theory and ε this gives D, continuous in the limit over a; at Frob_ℓ it is translation by ϖ_ℓ times Nm(ℓ).
Compatibility: D(γ_j^{p^{r_j}}) = D(x_j) = S_{x_j}ε(x_j), i.e. S_{x_j} = (1 + T_j)^{p^{r_j}}ε(γ_j^{−p^{r_j}}).
Freeness: ε(γ_j^{−p^{r_j}}) ∈ 1 + pℤ_p, so u(1 + T)^{p^r} − 1 is a unit times a distinguished polynomial of degree p^r; Weierstrass division gives the basis T^i, 0 ≤ i < p^r, in each variable.
acceptance: The rank is p^{Σ r_j}; Skinner–Wiles print Σ r_j (E1). Only freeness and finiteness are used.

nodes.title: Finiteness and freeness at a permissible maximal ideal
nodes.statement: If m is a permissible maximal ideal of T_∞(U, 𝒪), then (i) T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m is a torsion-free finite Λ_𝒪-algebra; (ii) if every element of U/(U ∩ F^×) acts on D^×\G^D(A_f) without fixed points, M_∞(U)_m and M⁺_∞(U)_m are free Λ_𝒪-modules of equal rank.
hypotheses: m permissible; for (ii) the fixed-point-free hypothesis of Skinner–Wiles Proposition 3.3.
proofSteps: T_∞(U, 𝒪) is finite and torsion-free over Λ′_𝒪 and semilocal complete (Skinner–Wiles Corollary 3.4, from PadicFamilies L5), so T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m is a direct factor, finite over Λ′_𝒪 and hence over Λ_𝒪.
Torsion-freeness over Λ_𝒪: if λt = 0 with 0 ≠ λ ∈ Λ_𝒪, the norm N(λ) ∈ Λ′_𝒪 is nonzero and kills t.

M_∞(U) is free over Λ′_𝒪 (Proposition 3.3, PadicFamilies L5); M_∞(U)_m is a direct summand, so free over Λ′_𝒪; a finite Λ_𝒪-module free over Λ′_𝒪 has depth dim Λ_𝒪, so it is free over the regular local ring Λ_𝒪 (Auslander–Buchsbaum).
Equal ranks: the ordinary pairing makes the m-parts of eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪) and eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪)⁺ mutually 𝒪-dual.
acceptance: T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m is only torsion-free and finite over Λ_𝒪; flatness is not asserted. Freeness is proved for M_∞(U)_m and M⁺_∞(U)_m under the fixed-point-free hypothesis.

nodes.title: Freeness over an auxiliary Δ_w-group
nodes.statement: Let w ∤ p be a place with U_w = GL₂(𝒪_{F,w}), Δ_w the Sylow p-subgroup of (𝒪_F/ℓ_w)^× and Δ′_w a complement; U′_w = {(a b; c d) ∈ GL₂(𝒪_{F,w}) : c ∈ ℓ_w}, U″_w = {(a b; c d) ∈ U′_w : ad^{−1} mod ℓ_w ∈ Δ′_w}, U′ = U′_w∏_{v≠w}U_v and U″ = U″_w∏_{v≠w}U_v. Then U′_a/U″_a ≅ Δ_w via (a b; c d) ↦ the image of (ad^{−1})_w (3.12); Δ_w acts on H⁰(X(U″_a), R) commuting with G(U″_a), T₀(p_i), T(ℓ) and S(ℓ) (ℓ ∤ pw), compatibly in a, and H⁰(X(U″_a), R)^{Δ_w} = H⁰(X(U′_a), R) (3.13). If every element of U′/(F^× ∩ U′) acts on D^×\G^D(A_f) without fixed points, then (i) M_∞(U″) and M⁺_∞(U″) are free Λ′_𝒪[[Δ_w]]-modules, and (ii) M_∞(U″)_{Δ_w} = M_∞(U′) and M⁺_∞(U″)_{Δ_w} = M⁺_∞(U′).
hypotheses: w ∤ p with U_w maximal; the fixed-point-free hypothesis is at level U′.
proofSteps: (3.12) and (3.13) are statements about the quaternionic sets and their change of level (R18.3).
#H⁰(X(U″_a), 𝒪/πⁿ)_{Δ_w} = #H⁰(X(U″_a), 𝒪/πⁿ)^{Δ_w} = #H⁰(X(U′_a), 𝒪/πⁿ), and the hypothesis gives #X(U″_a) = #Δ_w·#X(U′_a).
So H⁰(X(U″_a), 𝒪/πⁿ) is free over the local ring 𝒪/πⁿ[Δ_w]: its minimal number of generators is #X(U′_a) and its order is #(𝒪/πⁿ[Δ_w])^{#X(U′_a)}.
Pass to ordinary parts (e commutes with Δ_w) and to the limit with Proposition 3.3 (PadicFamilies L5).
acceptance: Freeness over the auxiliary group Δ_w and finite flatness over weight space are separate statements; this one needs the fixed-point-free hypothesis at level U′.

nodes.title: Skinner–Wiles deformation data and the residual extension ρ_c
nodes.statement: F is totally real of degree d, p odd, v_1, …, v_t the places above p with decomposition and inertia groups D_i ⊇ I_i and local degrees d_i, z_1, …, z_d the chosen complex conjugations, and χ : Gal(F̄/F) → k₀^× a character of a finite field of characteristic p with χ|_{D_i} ≠ 1 for every i and χ(z_j) = −1 for every j. A deformation datum is 𝒟 = (𝒪, Σ, c, ℳ): 𝒪 the ring of integers of a local field with finite residue field k ⊇ k₀; Σ a finite set of finite places containing those where χ ramifies and 𝒫 = {v_1, …, v_t}; a class 0 ≠ c ∈ H_Σ(F, k) := ker(H¹(F_Σ/F, k(χ^{−1})) → ⊕_i H¹(D_i, k(χ^{−1}))) (c is admissible); and ℳ ⊆ Σ∖𝒫 a set of places at each of which c is ramified or χ|_{I_v} ≠ 1. Through H¹(F_Σ/F, k(χ^{−1})) ≅ H¹(F_Σ/F(χ), k(χ^{−1}))^{Gal(F(χ)/F)} the class c gives a unique ρ_c : Gal(F_Σ/F) → GL₂(k), ρ_c = (1 *; 0 χ), with ρ_c(z_1) = diag(1, −1) and ρ_c(σ) = (1 c(σ); 0 1) for σ ∈ Gal(F_Σ/F(χ)); for admissible c, ρ_c|_{D_i} ≅ diag(1, χ).
hypotheses: χ|_{D_i} ≠ 1 at every v_i | p (p-distinguished) and χ totally odd.
proofSteps: ρ_c is nonsplit because c ≠ 0; as χ ≠ 1 its centraliser is the scalars, so ρ_c is Schur (the hypothesis of GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.2/universal-deformation-ring).
Admissibility kills the restriction of c to D_i, and χ|_{D_i} ≠ 1 splits the local extension.
acceptance: ρ_c is reducible but not split: the absolutely irreducible representability theorem is never used.

nodes.title: Nearly ordinary deformations of type 𝒟 and the ring R_𝒟
nodes.statement: A deformation of ρ_c is a complete local Noetherian ring A with residue field k and a strict equivalence class of continuous ρ : Gal(F̄/F) → GL₂(A) lifting ρ_c. It is of type 𝒟 if A is an 𝒪-algebra, ρ is unramified outside Σ and ∞, ρ|_{D_i} ≅ (ψ^{(i)}_1 *; 0 ψ^{(i)}_2) with χ = ψ^{(i)}_1 mod m_A for each i, and ρ|_{I_w} ≅ (1 *; 0 χ̃) for each w ∈ ℳ (χ̃ the Teichmüller lift). There is a universal deformation of type 𝒟, ρ_𝒟 : Gal(F_Σ/F) → GL₂(R_𝒟). For Q a finite set of places disjoint from Σ, type 𝒟_Q adds ramification at Q with det ρ unramified at Q, giving R_{𝒟_Q}; a deformation is 𝒟_Q-minimal if χ̃^{−1}det ρ is trivial on the torsion N_Σ of Gal(L_Σ/F), and R_{𝒟_Q} ≅ R^min_{𝒟_Q} ⊗_𝒪 𝒪[N_Σ] with ρ_{𝒟_Q} ≅ ρ^min_{𝒟_Q} ⊗ Ψ_Σ.
hypotheses: ρ_c Schur; Gal(F_Σ/F) satisfies Mazur's Φ_p (GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.2).
proofSteps: The conditions are deformation conditions (stable under the Schlessinger fibre products); R04.2 gives representability for Schur ρ_c.
The nearly ordinary condition at v_i is the ordered-flag condition with the χ-line as sub (LocalGaloisDeformationRings L8, requested).
Minimal twist: N_Σ is a finite p-group with p odd, so every character of it is a square; ρ^min ⊗ Ψ_Σ with Ψ_Σ : Gal(L_Σ/F) ↠ N_Σ is universal for type 𝒟_Q (Skinner–Wiles §2.3).
acceptance: Skinner–Wiles write 'det ρ is trivial on N_Σ'; since det ρ ≡ χ, the condition is on χ̃^{−1}det ρ.
The determinant is not fixed: R_𝒟 carries the Λ_𝒪-variables of deformation-iwasawa-algebra.

nodes.title: The presentation of R_𝒟 and its dimension bound
nodes.statement: For every deformation datum 𝒟 there are integers g, r with R_𝒟 ≅ 𝒪[[x_1, …, x_g]]/(f_1, …, f_r) and g − r ≥ d + δ_F − 2t − 3·#ℳ, where δ_F is the ℤ_p-rank of the Galois group of the maximal abelian pro-p extension of F unramified outside p (Skinner–Wiles Proposition 2.4). Hence every component of R_𝒟 has dimension ≥ 1 + d + δ_F − 2t − 3·#ℳ.
hypotheses: ρ_c Schur; the local nearly ordinary versal rings of Lemma 2.2 and Corollary 2.3 (requested from LocalGaloisDeformationRings L8).
proofSteps: Auxiliary type: deformations with det ρ = χ̃, unramified outside Σ, with universal ring R^aux_𝒟 ≅ 𝒪[[x_1, …, x_{g′}]]/(f_1, …, f_{r′}), g′ = h¹(F_Σ/F, ad⁰ρ_c), r′ ≤ h²(F_Σ/F, ad⁰ρ_c) (Mazur's presentation, GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.3).

At each v_i, R^{(i)}_ord is a quotient of the versal ring R^{(i)} by d_i + ε_i ≤ d_i + 2 elements (Corollary 2.3); the images J of these kernels in R^aux_𝒟 are generated by Σ_i(d_i + 2) = d + 2t elements (2.4).

Removing the determinant condition: R_{𝒟′} ≅ R^aux_𝒟/J ⊗̂_𝒪 𝒪[[Gal(L(Σ)/F)]] for 𝒟′ = (𝒪, Σ, c, ∅) (2.5) (R04.2/fixed-determinant-rings with n = 2, p ∤ 2), and 𝒪[[Gal(L(Σ)/F)]] ≅ 𝒪[[x_1, …, x_{δ_F}, y_1, …, y_s]]/(g_1, …, g_s) (2.6), s = dim_k H¹(D-free part) as in (2.2).
The ℳ-conditions: I = ker(R_{𝒟′} ↠ R_𝒟) is generated by a_v − 1, d_v − 1, c_v at a generator τ_v of tame p-inertia, 3·#ℳ elements (2.7).
Hence g = g′ + s + δ_F and r = r′ + s + d + 2t + 3·#ℳ; the global Euler characteristic formula for ad⁰ρ_c (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.3), with ρ_c odd, gives g′ − r′ ≥ 2d, whence the bound.
acceptance: The bound is on g − r for this particular presentation; dimension ≥ 1 + (g − r) follows because R_𝒟 is a quotient of a regular ring of dimension g + 1 by r elements.

nodes.title: R_𝒟 is topologically generated by matrix entries
nodes.statement: Fix a basis for ρ_𝒟 and let R′ ⊆ R_𝒟 be the 𝒪-subalgebra generated by the matrix entries a_σ, b_σ, c_σ, d_σ, m′ = m_𝒟 ∩ R′, R_1 = R′_{m′} and R̂_1 its completion. Then R̂_1 → R_𝒟 is surjective (Lemma 2.5). If 𝔭 ⊊ R_𝒟 is not maximal and 𝔭_1 = R_1 ∩ 𝔭, then dim R_1/𝔭_1 ≥ 1 (Lemma 2.6).
proofSteps: Lemma 2.5: ρ_1 over R̂_1 composes to ρ_𝒟; universality gives R_𝒟 → R̂_1/m_1 with kernel m_𝒟, so m_1R_𝒟 = m_𝒟 and dim_k R_𝒟/m_1R_𝒟 = 1; then R_𝒟 is generated as an R̂_1-module by one element (Matsumura, Theorem 8.4).
Lemma 2.6: if 𝔭_1 were maximal, 𝔭 would contain a uniformiser and ρ_𝒟 mod 𝔭 would have entries in k, so by universality 𝔭 = m_𝒟.
acceptance: Used in Proposition 2.11 to compare R_{𝒟_Q} with the pseudo-deformation ring.

nodes.title: Types A, B, B′ and C at a place w ∤ p
nodes.statement: For a field 𝒦 and ρ : Gal(F̄/F) → GL₂(𝒦) ramified at w ∤ p: type A if ρ|_{I_w} ≅ (1 *; 0 1) with * ≠ 0; type B if ρ|_{I_w} ≅ diag(φ, 1) with φ a finite character; type B′ if ρ|_{I_w} ≅ diag(φ, φ^{−1}) with φ finite; type C if ρ|_{D_w} = Ind_{F_{w²}}^{F_w} ψ for the unramified quadratic F_{w²}/F_w and ψ with ψ|_{I_w} ≠ ψ^{Frob_w}|_{I_w}, ψ|_{I_w} of p-power order and det ρ|_{D_w} of order prime to p. Type C occurs only in characteristic 0.

nodes.title: Wiles pseudo-representations and pseudo-deformations
nodes.statement: A (2-dimensional) pseudo-representation of Gal(F̄/F) into a topological ring A is ρ = {a, d, x} with continuous a, d : Gal(F̄/F) → A and x : Gal(F̄/F)² → A such that a(στ) = a(σ)a(τ) + x(σ, τ); d(στ) = d(σ)d(τ) + x(τ, σ); x(σ, τ)x(α, β) = x(σ, β)x(α, τ); x(στ, αβ) = a(σ)a(β)x(τ, α) + a(β)d(τ)x(σ, α) + a(σ)d(α)x(τ, β) + d(τ)d(α)x(σ, β); a(1) = 1 = d(1); a(z_1) = 1 = −d(z_1); and x(σ, g) = 0 = x(g, σ) for g ∈ {1, z_1}. Its trace is a + d and its determinant is a(σ)d(σ) − x(σ, σ). A representation with ρ(z_1) = diag(1, −1), ρ(σ) = (a_σ b_σ; c_σ d_σ), gives {a_σ, d_σ, b_σc_τ}. ρ_0 = {1, χ, 0} is the pseudo-representation of 1 ⊕ χ; a pseudo-deformation is (A, ρ) with A complete local Noetherian with residue field k and ρ mod m_A = ρ_0; a pseudo-datum 𝒟^ps = (𝒪, Σ) asks A to be an 𝒪-algebra and ρ to factor through Gal(F_Σ/F); type 𝒟^ps_Q adds places Q with det ρ unramified at Q.
hypotheses: p odd; the complex conjugation z_1 normalises the basis.
proofSteps: The identities for {a_σ, d_σ, b_σc_τ} expand the matrix product (checked in the Lean file).
The trace a + d is a 2-dimensional pseudocharacter (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0), 2 being invertible.
acceptance: This is the Wiles (generalized-matrix) formalism of the source, not the determinant formalism; the comparison with IHG.0 is only through the trace and determinant.
Every ρ_c, c ∈ H¹(F_Σ/F, k(χ^{−1})), has pseudo-representation ρ_0: the pseudo-deformation ring forgets c.

nodes.title: The universal pseudo-deformation ring
nodes.statement: The functor F_{𝒟^ps} of pseudo-deformations of type 𝒟^ps on complete local Noetherian 𝒪-algebras with residue field k satisfies Schlessinger's criteria; its tangent space has #F_{𝒟^ps}(k[ε]) = (#k)^r with r ≤ 4·#Gal(F(χ)/F) + 2(dim_k H¹(F_Σ/F(χ), k))² + 4 (Lemma 2.10). Hence there is a universal pseudo-deformation (R_{𝒟^ps}, ρ_{𝒟^ps}), and likewise R_{𝒟^ps_Q}.
hypotheses: k finite; Gal(F_Σ/F(χ)) has finite abelianised p-quotient (class field theory).
proofSteps: Schlessinger's (H1)–(H3) hold as for representations (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.2); only finiteness of the tangent space needs proof.
Over k[ε], a = 1 + εa_1, d = χ + εd_1, x = εx_1; restrictions to G_χ = Gal(F_Σ/F(χ)) give a_1|, d_1| ∈ Hom(G_χ, k) and x_1|_{G_χ×G_χ} ∈ Hom(G_χ, Hom(G_χ, k)), bounded by (#k)^{s² + 2s}.
The remaining data are cocycles vanishing on G_χ or constants on cosets of G_χ, giving the bound (#k)^{s² + 4s + 4·#Gal(F(χ)/F)} ≤ (#k)^{4·#Gal(F(χ)/F) + 2s² + 4}, since s² + 4s ≤ 2s² + 4.
acceptance: The stated bound is weaker than the one the proof gives; both suffice.

nodes.title: From pseudo-deformation rings to deformation rings
nodes.statement: For every deformation ρ of some ρ_c over an 𝒪-algebra A, the pseudo-representation associated to ρ in a basis with ρ(z_1) = diag(1, −1) is well defined (bases differ by diagonal conjugation) and of type (𝒪, Σ). Hence for a deformation datum 𝒟 with 𝒟^ps = (𝒪, Σ) there is a unique r_𝒟 : R_{𝒟^ps} → R_𝒟 inducing the pseudo-deformation of ρ_𝒟, and likewise r_{𝒟_Q} : R_{𝒟^ps_Q} → R_{𝒟_Q} and r^min_𝒟 : R_{𝒟^ps} → R^min_𝒟.
proofSteps: Two bases with ρ(z_1) = diag(1, −1) differ by a diagonal matrix, which fixes a_σ, d_σ and b_σc_τ; universality of R_{𝒟^ps} gives r_𝒟.
acceptance: r_𝒟 is not surjective in general: the pseudo-deformation ring does not see the extension class c.

nodes.title: Localising at irreducible one-dimensional primes
nodes.statement: If 𝔭 ⊆ R_{𝒟_Q} is a one-dimensional prime with ρ_{𝒟_Q} mod 𝔭 irreducible and 𝔭^ps = r_{𝒟_Q}^{−1}(𝔭), then R̂_{𝒟^ps_Q, 𝔭^ps} → R̂_{𝒟_Q, 𝔭} is surjective (Proposition 2.11). Consequently, for any prime Q ⊆ R_𝒟 with ρ_𝒟 mod Q irreducible and Q^ps = r_𝒟^{−1}(Q), dim R_{𝒟^ps}/Q^ps ≥ dim R_𝒟/Q, with equality if Q has dimension one (Corollary 2.12).
proofSteps: A = R_{𝒟_Q}/𝔭 is finite over A^ps = R^ps/𝔭^ps (A/m^psA is Artinian), so both have dimension one.

Irreducibility gives τ_0 with c_{τ_0} ∉ r(𝔭^ps); with ρ(σ_0) = (* u; * *), u a unit, the b_σ lie in the image after localising, so R′_{𝔭′} is the image of R^ps localised (R′ the subring generated by im r and the b_σ).
With Lemma 2.5, 𝔭^psR_{𝒟_Q,𝔭} = 𝔭R_{𝒟_Q,𝔭} and all residue fields agree, so the completed map is onto (Matsumura, Theorem 8.4).
Corollary 2.12 by induction on dimension through a one-dimensional 𝔭 ⊇ Q with ρ mod 𝔭 irreducible.
acceptance: Irreducibility of ρ mod 𝔭 is essential: at reducible primes the pseudo-deformation ring loses the extension data.

nodes.title: Lattices with nonsplit reduction and their extension classes
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete DVR with residue field k, K = Frac A, and ρ : Gal(F_Σ/F) → GL₂(K) irreducible with reduction (ρ̄^ss) 1 ⊕ χ. (i) There is a stable lattice L with ρ̄_L(σ) = (1 b_σ; 0 χ(σ)) nonsplit with scalar centraliser. (ii) For two such lattices the classes σ ↦ χ(σ)^{−1}b_i(σ) in H¹(F_Σ/F, k(χ^{−1})) are nonzero scalar multiples (Lemma 2.13). Consequently, if (A, φ) is a pseudo-deformation of ρ_0 unramified outside Σ with x not identically zero, there are 0 ≠ c ∈ H¹(F_Σ/F, k(χ^{−1})) and a deformation ρ_φ of ρ_c with pseudo-deformation φ, c unique up to a scalar (Corollary 2.14).
hypotheses: A a complete DVR with residue field k.
proofSteps: (i) In a basis with ρ(z_1) = diag(1, −1) rescale by diag(λ^{−n}, 1), n = min ord_λ(b_σ) < ∞ (irreducibility).
(ii) The change of lattice commutes with diag(1, −1), so is diag(1, a); unit entries force ord(a) = 0.
Corollary 2.14: ρ(σ) = (a(σ) x(σ, τ_0)/x(σ_0, τ_0); x(σ_0, σ) d(σ)) with ord x(σ_0, τ_0) minimal is an irreducible representation with pseudo-representation φ; apply the lemma.
acceptance: The extension class is determined only up to a scalar.

nodes.title: Lifting pseudo-deformations at one-dimensional primes
nodes.statement: (Proposition 2.15.) Let (R, ρ) be a pseudo-deformation of type (𝒪, Σ), 𝔭 ⊆ R a prime of dimension one with x(σ, τ) mod 𝔭 not identically zero, and k′ the residue field of the integral closure of R/𝔭. There are 0 ≠ c ∈ H¹(F_Σ/F, k′(χ^{−1})), unique up to a scalar, a local complete Noetherian 𝒪-domain R⁺ with residue field k′ and dim R⁺ = dim R, a local 𝒪-algebra map R ↪ R⁺, a dimension-one prime 𝔭⁺ ⊆ R⁺ over 𝔭, and a deformation ρ⁺ : Gal(F_Σ/F) → GL₂(R⁺) of ρ_c whose pseudo-deformation is induced from ρ. If moreover ℳ, Q ⊆ Σ satisfy (2.8) and ρ⁺ ⊗ ℒ (ℒ = Frac R⁺) satisfies (2.9), then ρ⁺ is of type 𝒟_Q for 𝒟 = (𝒪′, Σ∖Q, c, ℳ), 𝒪′ = 𝒪 ⊗_{W(k)} W(k′).
hypotheses: (2.8): ℳ ⊆ Σ∖𝒫 are places where ρ_c ramifies and Q ⊆ Σ∖(𝒫 ∪ ℳ) places where it is unramified. (2.9): the nearly ordinary shape at every v_i, the shape (1 *; 0 χ̃) on I_w for w ∈ ℳ, and det unramified on Q.
proofSteps: Corollary 2.14 gives c and ρ_𝔭 over the normalisation A of R/𝔭.

Blow up: R′ = R[α/β] with α/β a uniformiser of A, then R* = R′[i_1/i, …, i_r/i] with i an x(σ, τ) of minimal valuation; complete at the preimage of m_A and pass to a quotient by a minimal prime q⁺ (going down, Matsumura Theorem 9.5) to get a domain R⁺ with dim R⁺ = dim R.
In R⁺ the ideal IR⁺ = (i), i = x(σ_0, τ_0), and ρ⁺(σ) = (a(σ) x(σ, τ_0)/i; x(σ_0, σ) d(σ)) is a deformation of some ρ_{c′}; reduction mod 𝔭⁺ and Corollary 2.14 give c′ = c up to scalar.
acceptance: R⁺ is a new ring over R, not a quotient: pseudo-deformations are lifted after a finite birational modification.

nodes.title: The Λ_𝒪-algebra structures on deformation rings
nodes.statement: Let L_0 be the maximal abelian pro-p extension of F unramified outside 𝒫, I ⊆ Gal(L_0/F) generated by the images of the I_i, I_0 ⊆ I a maximal free ℤ_p-summand (rank δ_F), G_0 ⊇ I_0 a free summand of rank δ_F with generators the images of γ_1, …, γ_{δ_F} ∈ Gal(F̄/F) such that γ_i^{p^{r_i}} generate I_0, and y^{(i)}_1, …, y^{(i)}_{d_i} ∈ U_i generating a free summand of rank d_i. Λ_𝒪 = 𝒪[[T_1, …, T_{δ_F}, Y^{(i)}_j]] acts on R_𝒟 and R_{𝒟_Q} by T_i ↦ det ρ_𝒟(γ_i) − 1 and Y^{(i)}_j ↦ ψ^{(i)}_2(y^{(i)}_j) − 1, and on R_{𝒟^ps} by T_i ↦ det ρ^ps(γ_i) − 1 and Y^{(i)}_j ↦ (trace ρ^ps(g_iσ^{(i)}_j) − α_i trace ρ^ps(σ^{(i)}_j))/(β_i − α_i) − 1, where χ(g_i) ≠ 1 and α_i, β_i are the roots of X² − trace ρ^ps(g_i)X + det ρ^ps(g_i) with α_i ≡ χ(g_i). These are compatible with r_𝒟, with R_{𝒟′} ↠ R_𝒟 for Σ ⊆ Σ′, ℳ′ ⊆ ℳ, and with R_{𝒟^ps_2} → R_{𝒟^ps_1} for Σ_2 ⊇ Σ_1.
hypotheses: χ(g_i) ≠ 1 makes the roots distinct and β_i − α_i a unit (Hensel).
proofSteps: With ρ|_{D_i} upper triangular with diagonal (ψ_1χ̃, ψ_2) and g_i eigenvalues α_i = ψ_1χ̃(g_i), β_i = ψ_2(g_i), trace(g_iσ) − α_i trace(σ) = (β_i − α_i)ψ_2(σ) for σ ∈ D_i, so the two structures agree through r_𝒟.
acceptance: The T-variables use det(γ_i), the Y-variables the unramified-quotient character ψ_2; they match the Hecke side (R21.2/permissible-weight-algebra: 1 + T_j ↦ D(γ_j), 1 + Y ↦ T_y).

nodes.title: Hida's Galois representation over the nearly ordinary Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: Let F have even degree and Q a prime of T_∞(U, 𝒪), R = T_∞(U, 𝒪)/Q, L = Frac R. There is a continuous semisimple ρ_Q : Gal(F̄/F) → GL₂(L̄) with (3.4): (i) ρ_Q(z_1) = diag(1, −1); (ii) ρ_Q unramified at ℓ ∤ 𝔫p; (iii) trace ρ_Q(Frob_ℓ) = T(ℓ) mod Q; (iv) det ρ_Q(Frob_ℓ) = S(ℓ)Nm(ℓ) mod Q; (v) det ρ_Q(x) = S_xε(x) mod Q for x ∈ Z(U); (vi) ρ_Q|_{D_i} ≅ (ψ^{(i)}_1 *; 0 ψ^{(i)}_2) with ψ^{(i)}_2(y) = T_y mod Q for y ∈ 𝒪_{F,v_i}^× and ψ^{(i)}_2(λ_{𝔭_i}^{(𝔭_i)}) = T_0(𝔭_i) mod Q. Its pseudo-representation takes values in R.
hypotheses: [F : ℚ] even; 𝔫 the product of the ℓ with U_ℓ ≠ GL₂(𝒪_{F,ℓ}).
proofSteps: For ordinary π, Wiles' ρ_π with (3.2) (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.2); for nearly ordinary π twist to an ordinary π ⊗ ψ; local–global compatibility π_v ≅ π_v(ρ_π) (3.3) (R19.4).
Q algebraic of weight 2: ρ_Q = ρ_π for the π of any λ ∈ ℋ(Q).
Q minimal: glue the ρ_P over the dense set 𝒳(Q) (PadicFamilies L5/algebraic-primes-dense) as in Wiles [W2, Theorem 2.2.1].

(vi) for minimal Q: the semisimplification of ρ_Q|_{D_i} is ψ_1 ⊕ ψ_2 with ψ_2(y) = T_y; if ψ_1|_{I} ≠ ψ_2|_{I} choose τ_0 separating them and the dense 𝒴 ⊆ 𝒳(Q); at P ∈ 𝒵 the conjugated ρ′_Q is integral with nonsplit reduction, which forces the sub-character to be ψ_1; then ψ_2(λ) = T_0(𝔭_i) as in [W2, Lemma 2.2.4].
Non-minimal Q′ ⊆ Q: reduce the pseudo-representation of ρ_Q; (vi) by choosing a basis adapted to ψ_1 ≢ ψ_2 mod Q′.
acceptance: ρ_Q is only semisimple over L̄; integrality is for its pseudo-representation. Do not assert a representation over T_∞(U, 𝒪) or its localisation in the residually reducible case.

nodes.title: The pseudo-representation into T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m and the map R_{𝒟^ps} → T
nodes.statement: For a maximal ideal m of T_∞(U, 𝒪), patching the pseudo-representations of the ρ_Q over the minimal primes Q ⊆ m gives a pseudo-representation ρ^mod_m into T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m (3.5): unramified at ℓ ∤ 𝔫p, with trace ρ^mod_m(Frob_ℓ) = T(ℓ) and det ρ^mod_m(Frob_ℓ) = S(ℓ)Nm(ℓ). If m is permissible, ρ^mod_m is a pseudo-deformation of type 𝒟^ps = (𝒪, Σ), Σ the places with U_v ≠ GL₂(𝒪_{F,v}) together with 𝒫, giving (3.6) R_{𝒟^ps} → T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m, a map of Λ_𝒪-algebras.

proofSteps: T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m ↪ ∏_{Q ⊆ m minimal} T_∞/Q (reduced), and the functions a, d, x of the ρ_Q land in the image because their values are determined by traces, which lie in T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m.
Permissibility makes the residual pseudo-representation ρ_0 = {1, χ, 0}.
The Λ_𝒪-structures agree: det ρ^mod_m(γ_j) = D(γ_j) and ψ_2(y) = T_y (R21.2/permissible-weight-algebra).
acceptance: This is a pseudo-representation, not a representation, into T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m.

nodes.title: Permissible ideals are those with residual representation χ ⊕ 1
nodes.statement: A maximal ideal m of T_∞(U, 𝒪) satisfies (3.9) (R21.2/permissible-maximal-ideal) iff m ∩ 𝒪[[G(U)]] is the ideal of G(U) → Z(U) --χω^{−1}--> k, T_0(𝔭_i) − 1 ∈ m for all i, and the residual pseudo-representation of ρ^mod_m is χ ⊕ 1. There is at most one permissible maximal ideal, and modulo it S(ℓ) ≡ χω^{−1}(Frob_ℓ) for ℓ ∤ 𝔫p.
hypotheses: p odd, so 2-dimensional semisimple representations over k̄ are determined by traces and determinants.
proofSteps: (3.9) gives trace ≡ 1 + χ on Frobenii; the first condition gives det ≡ χ (S(ℓ)Nm(ℓ) ≡ χω^{−1}(ℓ)ω(ℓ)); Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt give ρ̄^ss ≅ χ ⊕ 1. The converse reads traces off.
Uniqueness: T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m is generated over Λ_𝒪 by T(ℓ), S(ℓ) (hecke-generation), whose residues are now fixed.
acceptance: This closes the deferral in R21.2/permissible-maximal-ideal.

nodes.title: Generation of T_m by Hecke operators and surjectivity of R_{𝒟^ps} → T_m
nodes.statement: Let m be a permissible maximal ideal of T_∞(U, 𝒪) and S a finite set of primes containing those with U_ℓ ≠ GL₂(𝒪_{F,ℓ}). Then T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m is generated over Λ_𝒪 by {T(ℓ), S(ℓ) : ℓ ∉ S} (Lemma 3.11). Hence for V ⊆ U the map T_∞(V, 𝒪)_m → T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m is surjective (Corollary 3.12) and (3.6) R_{𝒟^ps} → T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m is surjective (Corollary 3.13).
hypotheses: m permissible.
proofSteps: T^S (the Λ_𝒪-subalgebra generated by T(ℓ), S(ℓ), ℓ ∉ S) is local complete; by Chebotarev and continuity it contains trace ρ^mod(σ) and det ρ^mod(σ) for all σ.

With g_i ∈ D_i, χ(g_i) ≠ 1, and α_i ≡ 1, β_i the roots of X² − trace ρ^mod(g_i)X + det ρ^mod(g_i) in T^S (Hensel): T_y = (β_i − α_i)^{−1}(β_i trace ρ^mod(σ_y) − trace ρ^mod(g_iσ_y)) and T_0(𝔭_i) = (β_i − α_i)^{−1}(β_i trace ρ^mod(τ_i) − trace ρ^mod(g_iτ_i)) lie in T^S; the source omits the inverse (E3).
These identities are checked at each ρ_Q (Q minimal) with (3.4)(vi), T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m being reduced.
Corollaries: generators of T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m come from level V and from R_{𝒟^ps} (trace and determinant of ρ^ps).
acceptance: β_i − α_i ≡ χ(g_i) − 1 is a unit, so the corrected formula is legitimate in T^S.

nodes.title: The level of a minimal prime is controlled by its local type
nodes.statement: (Proposition 3.14.) Let w ∤ p and U_w ⊇ {(a b; c d) : c, a − 1 ∈ ℓ_w^s} for some s. For every minimal prime Q of T_∞(U, 𝒪) there is V ⊇ U such that Q is the inverse image of a prime of T_∞(V, 𝒪) and: (i) V_w ⊇ GL₂(𝒪_{F,w}) if ρ_Q is unramified at w; (ii) V ⊇ {c ∈ ℓ_w, a mod ℓ_w ∈ Δ_w} if ρ_Q is of type A; (iii) V ⊇ {a − 1, c ∈ ℓ_w^r} if of type B, ℓ_w^r the conductor of det ρ_Q|_{I_w}; (iv) V ⊇ {a − 1, c ∈ ℓ_w²} if of type C. (Proposition 3.15.) If ρ_Q|_{I_w} ≅ diag(φ, φ^{−1}) with φ of p-power order and U′ = ∏_{v≠w}U_v × U′_w, U′_w = {c ∈ ℓ_w, ad^{−1} mod ℓ_w ∈ Δ′_w}, there is a minimal Q′ ⊆ T_∞(U′, 𝒪) with ρ_{Q′} ≅ ρ_Q and the same inverse image in T_∞(U ∩ U′, 𝒪).
hypotheses: w ∤ p; Δ_w the Sylow p-subgroup of (𝒪_F/ℓ_w)^× and Δ′_w a complement.
proofSteps: ρ_P for P ∈ 𝒳(Q) has the same type as ρ_Q at w (through the pseudo-representation and irreducibility of ρ_P).
By Corollary 3.9 (PadicFamilies L5) it suffices that some λ ∈ ℋ(P) factors through level V, i.e. π ∈ Π^{n.o.}_2(V).
Local–global compatibility (3.3) and newform theory give a vector at w fixed by the required subgroup (Carayol's π_v ≅ π(σ_v), generalised in [W2]).
Proposition 3.15: ρ_P|_{I_w} ≅ diag(φ′, φ′^{−1}) with p-power order; π_w is principal series π(μ_1, μ_2) and a twisted new vector is U′_w-fixed.
acceptance: The subgroups depend on the type; type B′ is handled by Proposition 3.15, not 3.14.

nodes.title: Constraints on inertia characters at auxiliary levels
nodes.statement: (Lemma 3.16.) Let w ∤ p, Q a minimal prime and U_w ⊇ {c ∈ ℓ_w^r, a mod ℓ_w^r ∈ Δ_w}, r ≥ 1. (i) If ρ_Q|_{I_w} ≅ diag(φ_1, φφ_2) with φ_1, φ_2 of p-power order and φ nontrivial of order prime to p with conductor ℓ_w^r, then φ_1 and φ_2 are trivial. (ii) If ρ_Q|_{D_w} ≅ (εφ *; 0 φ) and (Nm(w) − 1, p) = 1, then φ|_{I_w} has finite order prime to p, and φ|_{I_w} = 1 if r = 1.
proofSteps: Reduce the characters modulo P ∈ 𝒳(Q) (orders are preserved) and compare conductors: (3.3) gives cond(π_w) = cond(φ_Pφ_{2,P})cond(φ_{1,P}), while the fixed vector gives cond(π_w) | ℓ_w^r and a central character of order prime to p on I_w.
(ii) cond(π_w) = max(ℓ_w, cond(φ_P)²) and the central character on I_w is φ_P².
acceptance: Used to bound the Galois side at the auxiliary levels of §3.6.

nodes.title: Twisting Hida families by finite characters
nodes.statement: (Lemma 3.17.) Let Q ⊆ 𝔭 be primes of T_∞(U, 𝒪) with Q minimal, R ⊆ L̄ a finite integral extension of T_∞(U, 𝒪)/Q and Ψ : Gal(F̄/F) → R^× of finite order. There are primes Q′ ⊆ 𝔭′ of T_∞(U ∩ U_1(cond^{(p)}(Ψ)²), 𝒪) with Q′ minimal, ρ_{Q′} ≅ ρ_Q ⊗ Ψ and ρ_{𝔭′} ≅ ρ_𝔭 ⊗ Ψ, cond^{(p)} the prime-to-p conductor.
hypotheses: Ψ of finite order.
proofSteps: For each P over 𝒳(Q), π ⊗ Ψ_P ∈ Π^{n.o.}_2(V_b) gives τ_P : T_∞(V, 𝒪) → R/P with (3.7): T(ℓ) ↦ T(ℓ)Ψ_P(Frob_ℓ), S(ℓ) ↦ S(ℓ)Ψ_P²(Frob_ℓ), S_x ↦ S_xΨ_P²(x), T_y ↦ T_yΨ_P(y), and T_0(𝔭_i) ↦ T_0(𝔭_i)Ψ_P(λ^{(𝔭_i)}_{𝔭_i}) (the source prints the inverse, E4).
The product map lands in the diagonal image of R, giving τ : T_∞(V, 𝒪) → R with (3.8); Q′ = ker τ is minimal by dimension, and 𝔭′ is the kernel through R/𝔭_1.
acceptance: Twisting changes the level only at the prime-to-p conductor of Ψ (squared).

nodes.title: Characteristic-p primes at auxiliary level come from level U′
nodes.statement: (Proposition 3.20.) With w, U′, U″ as in auxiliary-level-freeness (no hypothesis on U′/(U′ ∩ F^×)), let 𝔭 ⊆ T_∞(U″, 𝒪) be a prime with p ∈ 𝔭, det ρ_𝔭 = χ, ρ_𝔭|_{D_v} ≅ (ψ_1 *; 0 ψ_2) with (ψ_1/ψ_2)|_{I_v} of infinite order for some v | p, and ρ_𝔭 irreducible but not dihedral. Then 𝔭 is the inverse image of a prime of T_∞(U′, 𝒪).
hypotheses: F of even degree; ρ_𝔭 is the representation over the residue field of 𝔭 (R21.3/hida-family-representation).
proofSteps: Choose σ ∈ I_w with ω(σ) = 1, det ρ_𝔭(σ) = 1 and ρ_𝔭(σ) of infinite order, and (non-dihedral) τ with ω(τ) ≠ 1 and ρ_𝔭(σ^{n_0}τ) of infinite order; Chebotarev gives ℓ ∤ 6 unramified with Frob_ℓ close to σ^{n_0}τ.

At V′ = U′ ∩ U(ℓ), V″ = U″ ∩ U(ℓ) the action is free (R18.3), so M_∞(V″) is free over Λ′_𝒪[[Δ_w]] and M_∞(V″)_{Δ_w} = M_∞(V′) (auxiliary-level-freeness); since 𝔭 ⊇ (δ − 1 : δ ∈ Δ_w) in the ring T generated by Δ_w and T_∞(V″, 𝒪), T_∞(V″)/𝔭 = T_∞(V′)/im 𝔭.
The minimal prime Q ⊆ 𝔭_2 of T_∞(V′) is unramified at ℓ (types A and C are excluded by the choice of ℓ), so it comes from T_∞(U′) by level-type-control.
acceptance: No freeness hypothesis at level U′ is needed: the auxiliary prime ℓ supplies it.

nodes.title: The trace at tame inertia acts through δ_w + δ_w^{−1}
nodes.statement: (Lemma 3.21, Remark 3.22.) Assume T_∞(U, 𝒪) has a permissible maximal ideal m and χ(Frob_w) = 1 = ω(Frob_w). Let σ_w ∈ I_w generate the p-part of tame inertia, identified with an element of 𝒪_{F,w}^× by local reciprocity; δ_w = (σ_w 0; 0 1) generates Δ_w through (3.12). Then trace ρ^mod(σ_w) ∈ T_∞(U″, 𝒪)_m acts on M_∞(U″)_m as δ_w + δ_w^{−1}; so δ_w + δ_w^{−1} lies in T_∞(U″, 𝒪)_m, compatibly with change of U.
hypotheses: χ(Frob_w) = 1 = ω(Frob_w).
proofSteps: On a T_∞(U″)-eigenspace V ⊆ eH⁰(X(U″_a), 𝒪)_m ⊗ Q̄_p, π_w is not supercuspidal (that would force type C and χ(Frob_w) = −1).
If π_w is special, μ_1 is unramified and δ_w acts by 1; if principal series π(μ_1, μ_2) with μ_1μ_2 unramified, δ_w acts by μ_1(σ_w) or μ_1^{−1}(σ_w).
acceptance: The identity is on M_∞(U″)_m, where both T_∞(U″)_m and Δ_w act.

nodes.title: The Hecke rings T_{𝒟_Q}, T^min_{𝒟_Q} and modules M_{𝒟_Q}
nodes.statement: Assume L_p(F, −1, χω) is integral but not a unit, so permissible ideals exist (eisenstein-ideal-existence). For an augmented datum 𝒟_Q = (𝒪, Σ, c, ℳ)_Q with r(w) given by ℓ_w^{r(w)} ∥ cond(χ_w^{−1}), put U_{𝒟_Q} = ∏_w U_{𝒟_Q,w} with U_{𝒟_Q,w} = GL₂(𝒪_{F,w}) for w ∉ (Σ∖𝒫) ∪ Q; {c, a − 1 ∈ ℓ_w^{max(2, r(w)+1)}} for w ∈ Σ∖(𝒫 ∪ ℳ); {c ∈ ℓ_w^{max(1, r(w))}, a mod ℓ_w^{max(1, r(w))} ∈ Δ_w} for w ∈ ℳ; {c ∈ ℓ_w, ad^{−1} mod ℓ_w ∈ Δ′_w} for w ∈ Q. Then T_{𝒟_Q} = T_∞(U_{𝒟_Q}, 𝒪)_m with the pseudo-deformation ρ^mod_{𝒟_Q} of type 𝒟^ps_Q and surjections π_𝒟 : R_{𝒟^ps} ↠ T_𝒟, π_{𝒟_Q} : R_{𝒟^ps_Q} ↠ T_{𝒟_Q}; T^min_{𝒟_Q} = T_{𝒟_Q}/∩_{q ∈ ℳ^min(𝒟_Q)} q, where ℳ^min(𝒟_Q) (nonempty) is the set of minimal primes q with (χ̃^{−1}det ρ_q)|_{N_Σ} trivial; M_{𝒟_Q} = M_∞(U^min_{𝒟_Q})_m for the level U^min_{𝒟_Q} of Skinner–Wiles p. 55; π^min_𝒟 : R_{𝒟^ps} → T^min_𝒟.
hypotheses: F of even degree; L_p(F, −1, χω) integral and not a unit.
proofSteps: ρ^mod_{𝒟_Q} is of type 𝒟^ps_Q because of the level at Q (det unramified there) and Σ.
ℳ^min ≠ ∅: write det ρ^mod = Θ·Ψ·χ̃ with Ψ trivial on N_𝒟 and Θ trivial on the free part M_𝒟, choose Φ² = Θ, and use Lemma 3.17 to twist any q to q_Φ with ρ_{q_Φ} ≅ ρ_q ⊗ Φ^{−1}, which is minimal.
acceptance: χ̃^{−1}det ρ_q (not det ρ_q) is the character restricted to N_Σ.
The levels depend on the datum through r(w), Q and ℳ; M_{𝒟_Q} uses the auxiliary level U^min, not U_{𝒟_Q}.

nodes.title: T_{𝒟_Q} ≅ T^min_{𝒟_Q} ⊗ 𝒪[N_𝒟]
nodes.statement: (Proposition 3.23, Corollary 3.24, Lemma 3.25.) The splitting field L_Θ of Θ has Gal(L_Θ/F) ≅ N_𝒟, and there is an isomorphism of Λ_𝒪-algebras T^min_{𝒟_Q} ⊗_𝒪 𝒪[N_𝒟] ≅ T_{𝒟_Q} with T(ℓ) ⊗ n ↦ T(ℓ)·Φ(Frob_ℓ^{−1}·n) and S(ℓ) ⊗ n ↦ S(ℓ)·Θ(Frob_ℓ^{−1}·n). Hence T^min_{𝒟_Q} is a finite, torsion-free Λ_𝒪-algebra, and δ_w + δ_w^{−1} ∈ T^min_{𝒟_Q} maps to δ_w + δ_w^{−1} ∈ T_{𝒟_Q}.
proofSteps: Gal(L_Θ/F) ≅ N_𝒟: for a character ξ of N_𝒟, Lemma 3.17 gives P_ξ with ρ_{P_ξ} ≅ ρ_P ⊗ ξ, so ξ² = Θ mod P_ξ; as ξ² ranges over all characters (odd order), Θ|_{N_𝒟} is injective.
For q ∈ ℳ^min and ξ ∈ X(𝒟), Lemma 3.17 gives τ(q, ξ) : T_{𝒟_Q} → R(q, ξ) (3.14) and φ(q, ξ) : T^min ⊗ 𝒪[N_𝒟] → R(q, ξ) (3.15); ℳ′ = {q_ξ} = ℳ(𝒟_Q).
τ = ∏τ(q, ξ) and φ = ∏φ(q, ξ) have the same image, which gives the isomorphism.
acceptance: The twist is by Φ (a square root of Θ) on T(ℓ) and by Θ on S(ℓ).

nodes.title: Duality between M_∞ and M⁺_∞ over Λ
nodes.statement: (§3.7.) If U/(U ∩ F^×) acts freely on D^×\G^D(A_f): for each a, Hom_{𝒪[[G(U)]]}(M⁺_∞(U), 𝒪[[G(U_a)]]) = Hom_𝒪(eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪), 𝒪) = eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪)⁺ (λ_a, via the trace 𝒪[[G(U_a)]] → 𝒪 and the pairing), compatibly with tr(U_b, U_a); hence λ_∞ : Hom_{𝒪[[G(U)]]}(M⁺_∞(U), 𝒪[[G(U)]]) ≅ M_∞(U) and β_∞(U) : Hom_{Λ′_𝒪}(M⁺_∞(U), Λ′_𝒪) ≅ M_∞(U), natural for maps compatible with G(U) → G(V). At a prime 𝔭 of T_∞(U, 𝒪) with P = Λ′_𝒪 ∩ 𝔭, M̂_∞(U)_𝔭 ≅ Hom_{Λ̂′_P}(M̂⁺_∞(U)_𝔭, Λ̂′_P) (3.16); at a permissible m, M_∞(U)_m ≅ Hom_{Λ_𝒪}(M⁺_∞(U)_m, Λ_𝒪) (3.17).
hypotheses: Free action of U/(U ∩ F^×) on D^×\G^D(A_f).
proofSteps: λ_a: under free action M⁺_∞(U) ⊗_{𝒪[[G(U)]]} 𝒪[G(U_a)] = eH⁰(X(U_a), 𝒪); Frobenius reciprocity for the finite group G(U_a) identifies Hom_{𝒪[G]}(M, 𝒪[G]) with Hom_𝒪(M, 𝒪) through the coefficient of the identity; the pairing does the rest (R21.1).
𝒪[[G(U)]] = Λ′_𝒪[Z_0] with Z_0 finite, and Hom over Λ′_𝒪 and over 𝒪[[G(U)]] agree through the trace (again Frobenius reciprocity), giving β_∞.
(3.17): M_∞(U)_m, M⁺_∞(U)_m are free over Λ_𝒪 (Lemma 3.10) and Λ_𝒪 is free over Λ′_𝒪, so the trace Λ_𝒪 → Λ′_𝒪 identifies the two Hom's.
acceptance: Skinner–Wiles open §3.7 by quoting Proposition 3.3 for freeness over 𝒪[[G(U)]]; that rank statement is not justified (PadicFamilies E11), but the identifications above use only Frobenius reciprocity and Λ′_𝒪-freeness.

nodes.title: Ihara's lemma for definite quaternionic forms
nodes.statement: (Lemma 3.26.) Let U = ∏U_w with U_0(𝔫) ⊇ U ⊇ U(𝔫), w ∤ p with U_w = GL₂(𝒪_{F,w}), ℓ = ℓ_w, λ = λ^{(ℓ)}, V = U ∩ U_0(ℓ), (αf)(g) = f(g(1 0; 0 λ)) and ξ_1 : H⁰(X(U), R)² → H⁰(X(V), R), (f, g) ↦ f + αg (R an 𝒪-module). Then ker ξ_1 is annihilated by [U(1 0; 0 λ^{(q)})U] − 1 − Nm(q) for every prime q of F splitting completely in the ray class field of conductor 𝔫·∞.
hypotheses: q splits completely in the ray class field of conductor 𝔫∞.
proofSteps: For (f_1, f_2) ∈ ker ξ_1, f_1(gu) = f_1(g) for u ∈ δ^{−1}GL₂(𝒪_{F,w})δ, δ = diag(1, λ^{−1}); as SL₂(𝒪_{F,w}) and its δ-conjugate generate SL₂(F_w), f_1(gu) = f_1(g) for u ∈ U·SL₂(F_w) (3.18) (Diamond–Taylor, Lemma 2, generalised).

q has a totally positive generator π ≡ 1 mod 𝔫; by Eichler's norm theorem there is δ_0 ∈ D^× with ν_D(δ_0) = π, and strong approximation for the norm-one group G^D_1 (with G^D_1(F_w) = SL₂(F_w)) gives f_1(gγ) = f_1(g) for ν_D(γ) = π^{−1} (3.19) (both requested from R18.3).
U(1 0; 0 λ^{(q)})U is a union of Nm(q) + 1 cosets Ug_i with ν_D(g_i) = π, so the operator acts on f_1 by 1 + Nm(q).
acceptance: This is the Ihara-type statement at a place w ∤ p for definite quaternion algebras; the annihilator is Eisenstein-type.

nodes.title: Exactness at deeper Γ₁(ℓ^r)-level and the three-copy Ihara lemma
nodes.statement: (Lemmas 3.27–3.28.) With U^{(r)} = U ∩ U_1(ℓ^r), for r ≥ 1 the sequence H⁰(X(U^{(r−1)}), R) --δ--> H⁰(X(U^{(r)}), R)² --γ--> H⁰(X(U^{(r+1)}), R), δ(f) = (f, −αf), γ(f_1, f_2) = αf_1 + f_2, is exact; and the kernel of ξ : H⁰(X(U), R)³ → H⁰(X(U^{(2)}), R), ξ(f_1, f_2, f_3) = f_1 + αf_2 + α²f_3, is annihilated by [U(1 0; 0 λ^{(r)})U] − 1 − Nm(r) for every prime r splitting completely in the ray class field of conductor 𝔫∞.
proofSteps: Lemma 3.27: if αf_1 = −f_2 then f_1 = −α^{−1}f_2 is invariant under U′ = {a − 1 ∈ ℓ^r, c ∈ ℓ^{r−1}, b ∈ ℓ}, and U^{(r)} and U′ generate U^{(r−1)}.
Lemma 3.28: factor ξ through H⁰(X(U), R)⁴ → H⁰(X(U^{(1)}), R)² → H⁰(X(U^{(2)}), R) and apply Lemmas 3.26 and 3.27.
acceptance: Lemma 3.27 is used only through the three-copy statement of Lemma 3.28, in the level-raising arguments of §8.

nodes.title: No level raising at a non-Eisenstein auxiliary prime
nodes.statement: (Lemma 3.29.) Let (𝔫, p) = 1, 𝔭 ⊆ T_∞(U, 𝒪) a prime with p ∈ 𝔭, ρ_𝔭 irreducible and not dihedral, contained in a permissible m; let ℓ ∤ 𝔫p with p ∤ Nm(ℓ) − 1 and the ratio of the eigenvalues of ρ_𝔭(Frob_ℓ) not Nm(ℓ)^{±1}; U^{(0)} = U ∩ U_0(ℓ), U^{(1)} = U ∩ U_1(ℓ). Then (i) T_∞(U^{(1)}, 𝒪)_𝔭 ≅ T_∞(U^{(0)}, 𝒪)_𝔭 ≅ T_∞(U, 𝒪)_𝔭; (ii) M̂_∞(U^{(1)})_𝔭 ≅ M̂_∞(U^{(0)})_𝔭 ≅ M̂_∞(U)_𝔭² and M̂⁺_∞(U^{(1)})_𝔭 ≅ M̂⁺_∞(U^{(0)})_𝔭 ≅ M̂⁺_∞(U)_𝔭² as T̂_∞(U^{(1)}, 𝒪)_𝔭-modules.
hypotheses: The three conditions on ℓ; ρ_𝔭 irreducible and not dihedral.
proofSteps: (i): the surjections of Corollary 3.12 are isomorphisms after localisation because every minimal prime of T_∞(U^{(1)})_m in 𝔭 has ρ_Q unramified at ℓ (the eigenvalue condition), hence comes from level U (Proposition 3.14).

(ii): with ξ = lim ξ_a : M⁺_∞(U)² → M⁺_∞(U^{(1)}) and I = ker(T_∞(U^{(0)}) → T_∞(U)), Jacquet–Langlands and newform theory give eH⁰(X(U_a), K)[I_a] = im(ξ_a ⊗ K) (3.21); the snake lemma embeds the cokernel C into a quotient of lim ker(ξ_a ⊗ K/𝒪).

Lemma 3.26 and Chebotarev over the ray class fields F_a make trace ρ_m(σ) − 1 − ε(σ) kill C_m for σ ∈ Gal(F′/F_∞); if C_𝔭 ≠ 0, ρ_𝔭 would be reducible or dihedral. So M⁺_∞(U)²_𝔭 ≅ M⁺_∞(U^{(0)})[I]_𝔭 (3.20), whence (3.22), and M⁺_∞(U^{(0)}) = M⁺_∞(U^{(1)})[S(ℓ) − 1] gives (3.23).
acceptance: The hypothesis on ρ_𝔭(Frob_ℓ) is what prevents level raising at ℓ; without it T_∞(U^{(0)})_𝔭 can be larger.

nodes.title: Dimension of the reducible and diagonal loci
nodes.statement: (Lemmas 2.7–2.9.) With R^red_𝒟 = R_𝒟/I (I generated by the lower-left entries c_σ in a basis with ρ_𝒟(z_1) = diag(1, −1)) the universal reducible deformation ring: dim R^red_𝒟 ≤ 1 + 2δ_F + dim_k H_Σ(F, k); if q ⊆ R_𝒟 contains p, ρ_𝒟 mod q is reducible and its determinant has finite order, then dim R_𝒟/q ≤ δ_F + dim_k H_Σ(F, k). For the universal diagonal deformation (φ_1 0; 0 φ_2) of 1 ⊕ χ of type (𝒪, Σ), dim R^diag ≤ 1 + 2δ_F, and ≤ δ_F modulo a prime containing p with det of finite order.
proofSteps: Write G = Gal(L(Σ)(χ)/F) ≅ Δ × Γ × ℤ_p^{δ_F} (Γ a finite p-group) and A = ℤ_p[[G]]; reducible deformations factor through the maximal abelian pro-p extension M of L(Σ)(χ) unramified outside Σ∖𝒫 on which Δ acts through χ^{−1}.

H = Gal(M/L(Σ)(χ)) is an A-module generated by m = dim_k H_Σ(F, k) elements; a presentation 𝔞 → ⊕Ae_i ↠ H with e_m ↦ an element with ρ_c = (1 u; 0 1), u ≠ 0, gives the explicit universal reducible deformation over B ⊗̂ A_2 (Skinner–Wiles p. 17), from which the dimension bounds are read.
acceptance: These bounds are what make the reducible locus of small codimension after the base changes of §4.6.

nodes.title: Pro-modular primes and components of R_𝒟
nodes.statement: Let F have even degree, L_p(F, −1, χω) not a unit (so T_𝒟 exists), and 𝒟^ps = (𝒪, Σ). A prime q of R_𝒟 is pro-modular if φ_q : R_{𝒟^ps} → R_𝒟/q, the map of the pseudo-deformation of ρ_𝒟 mod q, factors through π_𝒟 : R_{𝒟^ps} ↠ T_𝒟, i.e. φ_q = θ_q ∘ π_𝒟 (4.1) for some θ_q : T_𝒟 → R_𝒟/q; then θ_q(T(ℓ)) = trace ρ_𝒟(Frob_ℓ) mod q for ℓ ∉ Σ. A deformation is pro-modular if its kernel is. If q is pro-modular so is every 𝔭 ⊇ q; a component of Spec R_𝒟 is pro-modular if its minimal prime is.
hypotheses: F of even degree; L_p(F, −1, χω) ∈ 𝒪 not a unit.
proofSteps: Specialisation: if q ⊆ 𝔭, compose θ_q with R_𝒟/q ↠ R_𝒟/𝔭.
acceptance: Pro-modularity is a statement about pseudo-deformations (traces), which is all that the Hecke side sees in the residually reducible case.

nodes.title: Good pairs, nice primes and the properties (P1), (P2)
nodes.statement: (F, 𝒟) is good if d is even; L_p(F, −1, χω) ∈ 𝒪 ∖ 𝒪^×; d > 2 + δ_F + 8(#Σ + dim_k H_{Σ_0}(F, k)); d_{v_i} > 2 + 2t + 7(#Σ + dim_k H_{Σ_0}(F, k)) for every v_i | p; and, for w ∤ p with ρ_c|_{I_w} ≠ 1, either χ|_{I_w} ≠ 1 or χ|_{D_w} = 1. A nice deformation (§2.3) is one over a one-dimensional domain of characteristic p, of type 𝒟_c, with ψ^{(i)}_1/ψ^{(i)}_2 of infinite order at each v_i. A dimension-one prime 𝔭 of T_𝒟 is nice for 𝒟 if ρ_𝔭 is irreducible, 𝔭 comes from T_{𝒟_c}, the class c′ of Lemma 2.13 for ρ_𝔭 is a scalar multiple of c, and a conjugate of the associated ρ is a nice deformation of type (𝒪′, Σ, c, ℳ); then R_𝒟 → A gives the nice prime 𝔭_𝒟. A prime of R_𝒟 is good if ρ_𝒟 mod 𝔭 is nice, and nice if moreover it is the inverse image of a pro-modular prime of R_{𝒟_c}. (P1): for every prime 𝔭 ⊆ T_𝒟 nice for 𝒟, every Q ⊆ 𝔭_𝒟 is pro-modular. (P2): R_{𝒟_c} has a pro-modular prime whose deformation is nice.
hypotheses: Σ_0 is the set of places where χ ramifies, with 𝒫; 𝒟_c = (𝒪, Σ_c, c, ℳ_c) as in §2.3.
proofSteps: For 𝔭 of dimension one with ρ_𝔭 irreducible, Lemma 2.13 gives ρ over the normalisation A of T_𝒟/𝔭 deforming some ρ_{c′}; (3.4) and permissibility (T_0(𝔭_i) ≡ 1) force ρ|_{D_i} to be split or (ψ_1 *; 0 ψ_2) with ψ_2 ≡ 1, so c′ is admissible and ρ is of type (𝒪′, Σ, c′, ∅).
acceptance: Goodness is preserved by shrinking Σ but not by base change; §4.6 exploits that a base change can become good.

nodes.title: Components of A/(f_1, …, f_r) meet in large dimension
nodes.statement: (Corollary A.2.) Let A be a local Cohen–Macaulay ring of dimension d and I = (f_1, …, f_r) with r ≤ d − 2. If the set of irreducible components of Spec(A/I) is partitioned into two nonempty sets 𝒞_1 ⊔ 𝒞_2, there are C_1 ∈ 𝒞_1 and C_2 ∈ 𝒞_2 with C_1 ∩ C_2 containing a prime of dimension d − r − 1.
hypotheses: A local Cohen–Macaulay; r ≤ d − 2.
proofSteps: Proposition A.1 (Raynaud, Corollaire 4.2): Spec(A/I) ∖ {m_A} is connected (recorded as a gap).

Induction on d − r: for d − r = 2 this is the proposition; otherwise pick a one-dimensional 𝔭 in C′_1 ∩ C′_2 and pass to A_𝔭 (Cohen–Macaulay of dimension d − 1), where the decomposition stays nontrivial.
acceptance: The linchpin of the Main Theorem: it produces pro-modular and non-pro-modular components meeting in large dimension.

nodes.title: The key proposition: every prime of R_𝒟 is pro-modular
nodes.statement: (Proposition 4.1.) Let 𝒟 be a deformation datum for F. If (F, 𝒟) is good and (P1) and (P2) hold for 𝒟 and 𝒟_c, then every prime of R_𝒟 is pro-modular.
hypotheses: (F, 𝒟) good; (P1) and (P2) for 𝒟 and 𝒟_c.
proofSteps: Case 𝒟 = 𝒟_c, step one: a component containing a nice prime is pro-modular by (P1); with (P2) some component is.

Step two: if a non-pro-modular component C_2 existed, Proposition 2.4 and Corollary A.2 give C_1 pro-modular with C_1 ∩ C_2 ⊇ Q of dimension d − 2t + δ_F − 3#ℳ_c; a minimal Q_1 over (Q, p, det ρ(γ_i) − 1) has dimension ≥ d − 2t − 3#ℳ_c − 1 > 1 + δ_F + (#Σ + dim H_{Σ_0}) by (G), so ρ mod Q_1 is irreducible (Lemma 2.6 with Lemmas 2.7–2.8).

Q_1 is pro-modular; by Corollary 2.12 (printed 'Proposition 2.12', E5) dim T/Q^mod_1 ≥ dim R/Q_1, and T is integral over Λ_𝒪; if Q^mod_1 contained all Y^{(i)}_j then dim ≤ d − d_i, contradicting (G), so some Y^{(i)}_1 ∉ Q_1.
A one-dimensional 𝔭 ⊇ Q_1 avoiding c_{σ_0} and the Y^{(i)}_1 is nice (ψ_2(y_1) = 1 + Y_1 of infinite order and det = χ), hence C_2 is pro-modular by step one: contradiction.

General 𝒟: good primes of R_𝒟 come from nice primes of R_{𝒟_c}, so components with a good prime are pro-modular; a minimal Q with a minimal Q_2 over (Q, I_2) of dimension ≥ d − 7#Σ − 1 lies in a good prime.
acceptance: The argument is dimension counting under (G); no R = T isomorphism is claimed at this stage.

nodes.title: A criterion for property (P2)
nodes.statement: (Proposition 4.2.) Let 𝒟 = (𝒪, Σ, c, ℳ) be a deformation datum. If (F, 𝒟) is a good pair and (P1) holds for every datum (𝒪′, Σ′, c′, ℳ′) with Σ′ ⊆ Σ and 𝒪′ ⊇ 𝒪, then (P2) holds for 𝒟.
hypotheses: (F, 𝒟) good; (P1) for all data with smaller Σ and larger 𝒪.
proofSteps: Step one: for 𝒟_0 = (𝒪′, Σ_0, c_0, ℳ_0) (Σ_0 the ramification of χ with 𝒫), T_χ = T_∞(U^χ, 𝒪)_m exists (Proposition 3.18, printed 3.14: E6); for a minimal prime Q of T_χ/(p, T_1, …, T_{δ_F}) the pseudo-representation has x ≢ 0 (otherwise a diagonal deformation, and Lemma 2.9 would give d ≤ 1 + δ_F, contradicting (G)); a one-dimensional 𝔭 ⊇ Q avoiding x(σ_0, τ_0) and the Y^{(i)}_1 gives, by Corollary 2.14, a nice pro-modular deformation of type 𝒟_0.
If c is a multiple of c_0 this gives (P2) for 𝒟_c. Otherwise let 𝒟_1 = (𝒪′, Σ_c, c_0, ℳ_1); (P2) for 𝒟_0 and (P1) with Proposition 4.1 make every prime of R_{𝒟_1} pro-modular.

Step two: cut R_{𝒟_1} by s − 2 linear conditions killing c and c_0 on generators of Gal(F_0(χ)/F(χ)) and by det ρ(γ_ℓ) − 1; by (G), (4.2) and Proposition 2.4 every minimal prime has dimension > δ_F + dim H_{Σ_c} (4.3), so ρ is irreducible there (Lemma 2.6). The reducible deformation with cocycle c_0 + cX gives a one-dimensional 𝔭; with A^tr = T_{𝒟_1}/Q^mod, a height-one P_0 ⊇ Σβ_i x(σ_i, ·) exists; Lemma 2.9 and Corollary 2.12 (printed Proposition 2.12: E5) exclude x ⊆ P_0, and (G) gives Y^{(i)}_1 ∉ P_0.
A one-dimensional 𝔭_1 ⊇ P_0 avoiding x(σ′, τ′) and the Y^{(i)}_1 gives ρ_1 (Corollary 2.14) with c_1 = c up to scalar, hence a deformation of type (𝒪, Σ_c, c, ∅).

Step three: ρ_1 is of type 𝒟_c (each w ∈ ℳ_c has χ|_{I_w} ≠ 1 or χ|_{D_w} = ω^{−1} = 1, (4.4); type B′ is impossible in characteristic p), and the prime 𝔭_2 of R_{𝒟_c} is pro-modular: Lemma 3.16, twisting (Lemma 3.17), the levels U′, U″ (4.8), Lemma 3.15 and Proposition 3.20 show 𝔭_3 comes from T_{𝒟_c}.
acceptance: The proof builds a pro-modular nice prime for 𝒟_c from the Eisenstein ideal of χ; this is where the p-adic L-function hypothesis of (G) enters.

nodes.title: Property (P1) holds for every deformation datum
nodes.statement: (Proposition 8.4.) If F has even degree and 𝒟 is a deformation datum for F, then (P1) holds for 𝒟: for every prime 𝔭 of T_𝒟 nice for 𝒟, every prime Q ⊆ 𝔭_𝒟 of R_𝒟 is pro-modular.
hypotheses: F of even degree.
proofSteps: Let Q ⊆ 𝔭_𝒟 be minimal, ρ = ρ_𝒟 mod Q and R = R_𝒟/Q. Choose a p-power-order ψ with χ̃^{−1}det(ρ ⊗ ψ) trivial on N_Σ; the kernel Q_1 of R_𝒟 → R for ρ ⊗ ψ factors through R^min_𝒟 and lies in 𝔭_𝒟.
Q_1 is pro-modular by Proposition 8.1 (nice-prime-r-equals-t: R̃^min_𝒟 ≅ T̃^min_𝒟 at nice primes).
Lemma 3.17 twists back: cond^{(p)}(ψ) is square-free and supported on Σ∖ℳ, so U_𝒟 ⊆ U_1(cond^{(p)}(ψ)²) and ρ is pro-modular; primes contained in 𝔭_𝒟 follow.
acceptance: The substance is Proposition 8.1; this node only records the reduction to the minimal case.

nodes.title: Skinner–Wiles Main Theorem
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real (any degree), 𝒟 = (𝒪, Σ, c, ℳ) a deformation datum for F and ρ : Gal(F_Σ/F) → GL₂(𝒪) a deformation of type 𝒟 with ρ irreducible, det ρ = ψε^μ (μ ≥ 1, ψ of finite order) and ρ|_{D_i} ≅ (χ̃ψ^{(i)}_1 *; 0 ψ^{(i)}_2) with ψ^{(i)}_2|_{I_i} of finite order for each i. If there is a totally real L/F with (i) solvable Galois closure over F, (ii) [L : ℚ] even, (iii) L permissible for 𝒟 and (iv) (L, 𝒟_L) good, then ρ ⊗ Q̄_p is the representation of a Hilbert modular newform.
hypotheses: The four conditions on L; ρ irreducible.
proofSteps: ρ_1 = ρ|_{Gal(F̄/L)} is of type 𝒟_L (permissibility). (P1) holds for all data over L (Proposition 8.4, L of even degree), so Propositions 4.1 and 4.2 make ρ_1 pro-modular: some λ : T_{𝒟_L} → 𝒪 induces its pseudo-representation.

λ satisfies the hypotheses of Proposition 3.7 (det and the local shape), giving a Hilbert newform f_1 over L with trace ρ_1(Frob_ℓ) = λ(T(ℓ)) (4.10); ρ_{f_1} (Wiles, (3.2)) has the same traces (4.11); ρ irreducible and odd makes ρ_1 irreducible, so ρ_1 ⊗ Q̄_p ≅ ρ_{f_1}.
Solvable base change for Hilbert modular forms ([GL]) descends f_1 to f over F with ρ_f|_{G_L} ≅ ρ_{f_1}; a finite character φ with ρ_f ⊗ φ ≅ ρ ⊗ Q̄_p finishes.
acceptance: Irreducibility of the characteristic-zero ρ is assumed even though ρ̄ is reducible (roadmap check).
The even-degree convention of §§3–4 is dropped: only L needs even degree.

nodes.title: Hypothesis H on relative class groups
nodes.statement: Hypothesis H: there are 0 < ε < 1/4 and c(ε) > 0 such that for every totally real field K and finite set S of finite places of K there is an imaginary quadratic extension L/K with prescribed behaviour at each place of S whose relative class group has p-rank at most c(ε)·[K : ℚ]^{1−ε}.

proofSteps: A hypothesis, not a theorem: Skinner–Wiles expect it to be easier than extending Washington's theorem to non-abelian fields.
acceptance: Theorem B is conditional on Hypothesis H; nothing downstream may use Theorem B unconditionally.

nodes.title: Skinner–Wiles Theorem A
nodes.statement: Let F be a totally real abelian extension of ℚ, p an odd prime and ρ : Gal(F̄/F) → GL₂(Q̄_p) continuous, irreducible and unramified outside finitely many places, with ρ̄^ss ≅ χ_1 ⊕ χ_2. If F(χ_1/χ_2) is abelian over ℚ, (χ_1/χ_2)(z) = −1 for every complex conjugation z, (χ_1/χ_2)|_{D_v} ≠ 1 for every v | p, ρ|_{D_v} ≅ (ψ^{(v)}_1χ̃_1 *; 0 ψ^{(v)}_2χ̃_2) with ψ^{(v)}_2 factoring through a pro-p group of F_v and ψ^{(v)}_2|_{I_v} of finite order, and det ρ = ψε^{k−1} with k ≥ 2 and ψ of finite order, then ρ is the representation of a Hilbert modular newform.
hypotheses: F and F(χ_1/χ_2) abelian over ℚ; p odd.
proofSteps: ρ_1 = ρ ⊗ χ̃_2^{−1} with χ = χ_1/χ_2 is, in a suitable lattice, a deformation of type 𝒟 = (𝒪, Σ, c, ∅) for an admissible c (Lemma 2.13 and the local hypotheses); it remains to build L as in the Main Theorem.

Take E/F even, abelian over ℚ and permissible (E = F·E′ with E′ a real cyclic field where p splits and the primes of Σ are inert), ℓ ∤ p·#k^× odd, E_n the ℤ/ℓ^n-layer of the cyclotomic ℤ_ℓ-extension; #Σ_n, #𝒫_n stabilise (4.12), and by Washington's theorem the p-parts of the class groups of E_n(χ) and E_n stabilise (4.13) (gap).

Adjoin abelian p-extensions L_n/E_n ramified at a set S_n of e_n + c_n + 1 places with χ(Frob_w) = 1 and p^{e_n + c_n + 1} | Nm(w) − 1 (4.16); congruences of p-adic L-functions give L_p(L_n, −1, χω) ∈ 𝒪 ∖ 𝒪^× (4.17), and dim H_{Σ_0}(L_n, k) ≤ p^{e_n+2c_n+1}(r_n + e_n + c_n + 1) (4.18).
For n_0 large (4.19) and Waldschmidt's δ_L ≤ d_L/2 (gap), L = L_{n_0} satisfies (G) (4.20), so the Main Theorem applies.
acceptance: The abelian hypotheses are exactly what Washington's theorem needs; for non-abelian F one uses Theorem B.

nodes.title: Skinner–Wiles Theorem B (conditional on Hypothesis H)
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real and assume Hypothesis H for all solvable totally real extensions of F. Let p be odd and ρ : Gal(F̄/F) → GL₂(Q̄_p) continuous, irreducible and unramified outside finitely many places with ρ̄^ss ≅ χ_1 ⊕ χ_2. If (χ_1/χ_2)(z) = −1 for every complex conjugation z, (χ_1/χ_2)|_{D_v} has even order for every v | p, ρ|_{D_v} has the nearly ordinary shape of Theorem A with ψ^{(v)}_2 through a pro-p extension of F_v and finite order on I_v, and det ρ = ψε^{k−1} (k ≥ 2, ψ finite), then ρ is the representation of a Hilbert modular newform.
hypotheses: Hypothesis H for all solvable totally real extensions of F.
proofSteps: By base change it suffices to treat F⁺, the maximal totally real subfield of F(χ); there χ|_{D_v} ≠ 1 for v | p and χ is quadratic.
As in Theorem A, find a solvable permissible E of even degree with L_p(E, −1, χω) ∈ 𝒪 ∖ 𝒪^× and the ramification condition (4.21).

Hypothesis H gives totally imaginary quadratic characters ψ over E with prescribed local behaviour and small relative class groups; the splitting field of χψ is a totally real quadratic L_1/E, and iterating gives L_n with (4.22).
For n_0 as in (4.23), L = L_{n_0} satisfies (4.24) and (4.25) (with Waldschmidt's bound), so (L, 𝒟_L) is good (the proof's list says '(vi)' for condition (iv): E7).
acceptance: Conditional: every consumer must carry Hypothesis H.

nodes.title: Skinner–Wiles formal patching data over k[[T]]
nodes.statement: Let k be a finite field of characteristic p, A = k[[T]] with fraction field K, 𝓛 = {N} strictly increasing odd integers with 0, and n ≥ 1. A_N = A[[s_1, …, s_n]]/(s_i^{N+1}), B_N = A[[t_1, …, t_n]]/(t_i^{(N+1)/2}) ⊆ A_N via t_i ↦ (1 + s_i) + (1 + s_i)^{−1} − 2. A patching datum is: rings R^{(N)} = A[[x_1, …, x_m]]/𝔞^{(N)} (m independent of N) finite free over A with 𝔞^{(N)} ⊆ (x_i), surjections R^{(N)} ↠ R^{(0)}, B_N-algebra structures, and for odd 0 ≤ a ≤ N rings R^{(N)}_a with (5.2)–(5.5) (𝔭^{d(a)} = 0 in R^{(N)}_a, 𝔭/𝔭² ≅ Aⁿ ⊕ Tor with Tor bounded independently of N and a); trace subrings R^{tr(N)} = A[[y_1, …, y_m]]/𝔟^{(N)} with (5.6)–(5.8) (the cokernel of 𝔮/𝔮² → 𝔭/𝔭² bounded independently of N); modules M^{(N)} free over A of rank r·rank_A A_N, compatible over A_N, with quotients M^{(N)}_a satisfying (5.9)–(5.10) (in particular M^{(N)}_a ⊗ K free over A_a ⊗ K with (s_i)-coinvariants M^{(0)} ⊗ K, and z·M^{(0)} ⊆ M^{(N)}_0 for a fixed z with ord_T(z mod 𝔮^{(0)}) ≠ 0); and x^{(N)} ∈ R^{tr(N)} annihilating ker(M^{(N)}_a/(s_i) ↠ M^{(N)}_0) with ord_T(x^{(N)} mod 𝔮^{(N)}) = t independent of N (5.11).
hypotheses: A = k[[T]] (residue fields of the rings are not finite: the patching is over A, not over 𝒪).
proofSteps: A list of axioms; the verification in the arithmetic case is minimum-level-r-equals-t.
acceptance: The patching is performed on deformation rings, not on Hecke rings (contrast with Taylor–Wiles); only B_N (the t_i), not A_N, acts naturally on R_∞ (Remark 5.10).

nodes.title: The formal patching theorem
nodes.statement: (Lemmas 5.1–5.6, Propositions 5.7–5.9.) For a patching datum: R_∞ := lim_a R_a ⊗ K ≅ K[[x_1, …, x_n]] and M_∞ is a free R_∞-module (Lemma 5.6); dim_K(R^{(N)}_1 ⊗ K) ≥ 2ⁿ dim_K(R^{(N)}_0 ⊗ K) for N ≫ 1 (Proposition 5.7); M^{(0)} ⊗_A K ≅ (R^{(0)} ⊗_A K)^e with e = rk_{R_∞}(M_∞) (Proposition 5.8); and R^{(0)} ⊗_A K is a complete intersection as a K-algebra (Proposition 5.9).
hypotheses: The axioms of formal-patching-datum.
proofSteps: Lemma 5.2: T^{E(a)}R^{(N)}_a ⊆ R^{tr(N)}_a with E(a) independent of N, by (5.5) and (5.8) and induction on the power of 𝔭; Lemma 5.3: T^{d(a)(t+d_1)} kills kernel and cokernel of M^{(N)}_a/(T^c, s_i) → M^{(0)}/T^c.

Level-(a, c) structures J(N, a, c) take finitely many values up to isomorphism, so nested infinite subsequences 𝓛_a give inverse limits R_a, R^tr_a, M_a; Lemma 5.4: R^tr_a ⊗ K = R_a ⊗ K, a quotient of K[[x_1, …, x_n]], and M_a ⊗ K free over A_a ⊗ K of rank r with (s_i)-coinvariants M^{(0)} ⊗ K.
Lemma 5.6: K[[s]]^r ≅ M_∞, Krull dimension gives R_∞ = K[[x]], Auslander–Buchsbaum (R03.3) gives freeness.

Proposition 5.7 via de Smit–Rubin–Schoof Lemma 4.1 (R03.3) and Auslander–Buchsbaum twice; Proposition 5.8 by comparing generator counts (5.15)–(5.17); Proposition 5.9: N = Σs_iM_∞ ≅ 𝔞^e with 𝔞 = ker(R_∞ → R^{(0)} ⊗ K), so et ≤ en, t = n and R^{(0)} ⊗ K is a complete intersection.
acceptance: The conclusions are after ⊗_A K (the generic fibre over A = k[[T]]), not integral.

nodes.title: Irreducibility and eigenvalue lemmas in characteristic p
nodes.statement: (Lemmas 6.1–6.5.) Let A ≅ k[[λ]] with fraction field K and ρ : G_Σ → GL₂(A) with (6.2): ρ ⊗ K̄ irreducible and of type A, B or unramified at each w ∤ p; ρ mod λ = ρ_c; Σ ⊇ primes above p and where ρ̄ ramifies; ρ of type A or B exactly where ρ̄ is; det ρ = χ; ρ|_{D_v} ≅ (χ_1 *; 0 χ_2) with χ_1/χ_2 of infinite order for each v | p. Then W = ad⁰ρ ⊗ K̄ is irreducible (ρ ⊗ K̄ not dihedral); ρ ⊗ K̄|_{Gal(F_Σ/F⁺)} is neither reducible nor dihedral (F⁺ ⊆ F′ the real subfield of the splitting field of det ρ with μ_{p^∞}); there are σ ∈ Gal(F_Σ/F′) and σ ∈ Gal(F_Σ/F⁺) ∖ Gal(F_Σ/F′) whose ρ-eigenvalues have infinite order and lie in A; ρ ⊗ K̄ is irreducible on every finite-index normal subgroup of Gal(F_Σ/F⁺); and there is N_2 with λ^{n−(a−N_2)}𝒯_n ⊆ M for every submodule M ⊆ 𝒯_n = ad⁰ρ/λⁿ containing an m with λ^a m ≠ 0, a > N_2.
hypotheses: (6.2)(i)–(vi); characteristic of K is p.
proofSteps: Self-duality of W and the infinite-order element σ ∈ D_v force any decomposition of W to come from a quadratic character, making ρ induced; ρ|_{D_v} not split contradicts that (Lemma 6.1).
Lemma 6.3: finite-order eigenvalues in characteristic p on a pro-p image are 1; a unipotent τ and trace comparisons force triangularity otherwise; Hensel gives eigenvalues in A.
Lemma 6.5: A[G]x ⊇ λ^r ad⁰ρ with r = r(x) continuous, hence bounded.
acceptance: All representations here are over a characteristic-p DVR: finite-order means p-power, and 'dihedral' is tested over K̄.

nodes.title: Auxiliary prime sets in characteristic p
nodes.statement: (Proposition 6.10, with (6.3)–(6.11) and Lemmas 6.7–6.9.) With ρ as in char-p-adjoint-irreducibility and σ ∈ Gal(F_Σ/F′) whose ρ-eigenvalues lie in A and have infinite order, there is r = r(ρ) such that for every m > 0 there are infinitely many sets Q = {w_1, …, w_r} with Nm(w_i) ≡ 1 mod p^m, ρ(Frob_{w_i}) ≡ ρ(σ) mod λ^m, and lim_n H_{Σ_Q}(𝒯_n) ≅ (K/A)^r ⊕ X_{Σ_Q} with #X_{Σ_Q} < C(σ, r) independent of Q (Σ_Q = Σ_0 ∪ Q).
hypotheses: (6.2); the Selmer groups H_Σ(𝒯_n) use L_w = ker(H¹(D_w, 𝒯_n) → H_w(𝒯_n)) with H_v the ordinary condition at v | p and H_w the type-A/B condition at ramified w ∤ p.
proofSteps: Wiles' formula #H_Σ(𝒯_n)/#H*_Σ(𝒯_n) = h_∞∏h_w (6.3) ([W1, Proposition 1.6], generalised to totally real F; Poitou–Tate, ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4–R02.5); h_∞ ≍ #(A/λⁿ)^{2[F:ℚ]}, h_w ≍ 1 at type A/B places, h_v ≍ #(A/λⁿ)^{−2[F_v:ℚ_p]} (6.4)–(6.8), whence #H_Σ ≍ #H*_Σ·∏_{w∈Σ′}#H⁰(D_w, 𝒯_n(1)) (6.9).
(6.10)–(6.11) and Lemmas 6.7–6.8: the direct limits are (K/A)^r ⊕ finite.
Lemma 6.9 (after [W1, Proposition 1.11]): λ^{N_1} kills H¹(E_∞/F, 𝒯_n(1)) — a measure argument on the map σ ↦ lim σ^{1+p^n} with Lemma 6.4.
Choose primes w_j inductively by Chebotarev (GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5) so that each kills a (K/A) summand of lim H*: after r steps lim H*_{Σ_r} is bounded, and (6.9) gives the claim.
acceptance: The coefficients are the characteristic-p DVR A: R04.5's finite-coefficient Taylor–Wiles primes are used only for the Chebotarev choice; the counting is done here.

nodes.title: The map ψ(𝒟, 𝔭) from deformation to Hecke rings
nodes.statement: (Lemma 7.1, Remark 7.2.) Let F have even degree, 𝒟 a deformation datum and 𝔭 ⊆ T_𝒟 nice for 𝒟 (so 𝔭 comes from T^min_𝒟; A = the normalisation of T^min_𝒟/𝔭 ≅ k′[[λ]]). With Λ̃_𝒪 = 𝒪′[[W_1, …, W_m]] finite free over Λ_𝒪 (7.2), tilded rings R̃ = R ⊗_{Λ_𝒪} Λ̃_𝒪 and localisations-completions at primes 𝔭̃ over 𝔭, there is a natural local surjection ψ(𝒟, 𝔭) : (R̃^min_𝒟)_{𝔭̃} ↠ (T̃^min_𝒟)_{𝔭̃} with trace ρ^min(Frob_ℓ) ⊗ 1 ↦ T(ℓ) ⊗ 1 and det ρ^min(Frob_ℓ) ⊗ 1 ↦ S(ℓ)Nm(ℓ) ⊗ 1 for ℓ ∉ Σ; the same holds for the auxiliary data 𝒟_Q.
hypotheses: 𝔭 nice for 𝒟.
proofSteps: For each minimal Q ⊆ 𝔭̃ and each two-dimensional prime 𝔔 of the normalisation B of T̃/Q over a regular point of Λ̃_{𝒪,P}, Proposition 2.15 lifts the pseudo-deformation to (𝒪_j, Σ, c, ℳ)-minimal deformations ρ_j, giving maps from R̃^min.

Injectivity of the completed products (7.4)–(7.5) and Proposition 2.11 make R̃^ps → T̂_{𝔭_i} factor through R̃^min; the image in ∏(T̃^min)_{𝔭̃}/Q is that of (T̃^min)_{𝔭̃}, giving the surjection (7.6).
acceptance: There is no natural map R^min → T^min: ψ exists only after localising and completing at a nice prime.

nodes.title: R = T at nice primes of minimal level
nodes.statement: (Proposition 7.3.) Let F be totally real of even degree, 𝒟 = 𝒟_c and 𝔭 ⊆ T_𝒟 nice for 𝒟. Then (i) ψ(𝒟, 𝔭) : (R̃^min_𝒟)_{𝔭̃} → (T̃^min_𝒟)_{𝔭̃} is an isomorphism and (R̃^min_𝒟)_{𝔭̃} is a complete intersection over Λ̃_{𝒪,P} and reduced; (ii) M̃_{𝒟,𝔭̃} is a free (T̃^min_𝒟)_{𝔭̃}-module.
hypotheses: F of even degree; 𝒟 = 𝒟_c (Σ = Σ_c, ℳ = ℳ_c = Σ_c ∖ 𝒫); 𝔭 nice.
proofSteps: Patching data: N^{(0)} = im(M̃_𝒟 → (M̃_𝒟)_{𝔭̃}/P) (7.7); R^{(0)}, R^{tr(0)} as images in (R̃^min)_{𝔭̃}/(𝔭̃F_0, P) (7.8)–(7.9) with F_0 the Fitting ideal; for odd N the sets Q_N of Proposition 6.10 give R^{(N)}_a, R^{tr(N)}_a (7.11)–(7.13) and M^{(N)}_a (7.10), with s_i = δ_{w_i} − 1 (Lemma 3.21).

Verification of (5.2)–(5.11): generator bounds from dim H¹(F_{Σ∪Q}/F, ad⁰ρ_c) and Lemma 2.10; freeness (5.10vi) via Lemma 3.19 after auxiliary Γ₁(ℓ_1⋯ℓ_s)-level at primes chosen by (7.15)–(7.16) with Lemma 3.29 and Corollary 3.6; the element x^{(N)} of (5.11) built in (7.21)–(7.25).

Proposition 5.9 gives R^{(0)} ⊗ K a complete intersection and Proposition 5.8 makes M^{(0)} ⊗ K free; with Lemma 5.2 (R^{tr(0)} ⊗ K ≅ R^{(0)} ⊗ K) and the surjection to (T̃^min)_{𝔭̃}/P, ψ mod P is an isomorphism; freeness of M̃ over Λ̃_{𝒪,P} lifts this to ψ and gives F_0 = 0 ((7.27)–(7.28)).
acceptance: Complete intersection and freeness are proved at the localisation-completion at 𝔭̃, not globally.
